title: Quoted outbound 'Unsubscribe:' footer in normal replies auto-suppresses every contact who replies
description: Every outbound campaign/follow-up email gets compliance.FooterText appended, which contains the literal line 'Unsubscribe: <url>' (unsubscribe.go:143). Gmail's extractBody returns the raw text/plain part with no quoted-history stripping, and virtually every mail client quotes the original message below the reply. persistIncoming then runs compliance.LooksLikeOptOut(body) on that full body (poller.go:226), which does a plain strings.Contains on 'unsubscribe' (unsubscribe.go:114,122). Result: a warm 'yes, send me pricing' reply that quotes the original email matches the keyword and the contact is MarkUnsubscribed('reply_keyword') — exactly the false positive the function's own comment says must not happen ('false positives lock a contact out of further outreach'). The same unstripped body (quoted footer + the sender's own enthusiastic pitch) is also what classifyReply feeds the AI, contaminating both the sentiment score and the intent tags (the model can read 'unsubscribe' in the quoted footer).
suggestion: Strip quoted history before both the keyword scan and classification: drop lines starting with '>', everything from a line matching /^On .* wrote:$/, and everything below the own-footer marker ('---' / 'Unsubscribe:'). At minimum, run LooksLikeOptOut only on the new-text portion and add a regression test whose body is a positive reply quoting FooterText output.
verifyNote: Confirmed: scheduler.go:106 and engine.go:501 append FooterText containing the literal "Unsubscribe: <url>" line (unsubscribe.go:140-143); gmail.go:286-311 extractBody returns the raw text/plain part with no quote stripping anywhere in the backend; poller.go:226 then runs LooksLikeOptOut (substring match on "unsubscribe", unsubscribe.go:113-122) on the full body, so any reply quoting the original email — the default in every major mail client — triggers MarkUnsubscribed("reply_keyword"), and suppression is enforced at scheduler.go:61, engine.go:416, drafter.go:63, permanently locking out warm leads. The suggested fix (strip quoted history/own footer before both the keyword scan and the classifyReply call at poller.go:201, plus a regression test quoting FooterText output) is correct; also scope the keyword match to the new-text portion only.

title: Classifier failure is silently persisted as authoritative 'neutral' — unsubscribe/OOO/wrong_contact routing permanently lost
description: classifyReply returns the neutral() default (score 0, label neutral, legacy neutral, zero tags) on every failure path — AI router error, timeout, invalid JSON — without any logging. That default is then written by SetInboundClassification exactly as if it were a real classification, and because messages are idempotent by external_id the message is never re-classified. A transient AI outage therefore converts an 'unsubscribe' or hostile reply into a stored neutral with no tags: ResolveIntentRouting sees no tags, ResolveReplyBranch sees neutral, and handleReplyBranch auto-drafts a friendly follow-up instead of suppressing the contact (the English-only LooksLikeOptOut keyword backstop misses non-obvious or non-English phrasing — and this is an export-outreach product). There is no marker distinguishing 'classified neutral' from 'classification failed', so facets, lessons (matched on the neutral bucket), and the Simulation-vs-production comparison are all silently polluted.
suggestion: On classify error: log it, leave sentiment columns NULL (or write a distinct 'unclassified' label) instead of fabricating neutral, and enqueue a retry (e.g. re-classify on next poll tick for messages with NULL sentiment and non-empty body). Only persist neutral when the model actually said neutral.
verifyNote: Confirmed: poller.go:257-264 returns neutral() on AI error/bad JSON with no logging, poller.go:201-202 + repository.go:274-287 persist it indistinguishably from a real classification, and poller.go:154-158 idempotency means it is never re-classified; with zero tags and neutral sentiment, engine.go:165-212 skips MarkUnsubscribed and takes the auto-draft branch, while the English-only keyword backstop (unsubscribe.go:113-121) is the sole remaining opt-out catch. P0 stands because a missed unsubscribe leaves the contact un-suppressed for future automated sends (compliance exposure) with no log trail; the suggested fix is correct — log the failure, persist NULL/'unclassified' instead of fabricated neutral, and re-classify NULL-sentiment inbound messages on a later poll tick (note: also handle the p.ai==nil case, which currently neutrals every reply silently).

title: Race: last_direction flips to 'in' before classification commits, so the engine can branch on the previous reply's sentiment/tags
description: persistIncoming calls UpdateLast (sets conversations.last_direction='in') at line 196, then makes the AI classification call (seconds of latency) and only afterwards persists it via SetInboundClassification (line 202). The engine's processOne enters the reply branch purely on LastDirection=='in' (engine.go:117) — it does not wait for the poller's wake at line 212 — and waiting no_reply runs are re-bumped +60s on every unmatched trigger (engine.go:135), i.e. they are due on essentially every scheduler tick. If a tick lands inside the AI-latency window, handleReplyBranch routes on the previous reply's last_inbound_sentiment and stale conversation_tags (e.g. drafts an engagement to an unsubscribe reply), then completes the run with StoppedOnReply; the wake at line 212 is then a no-op because the run is no longer active, so the correct classification is never acted on.
suggestion: Reorder persistIncoming: classify and commit SetInboundClassification first, then UpdateLast + wake the run in that order (or do all three in one transaction). Alternatively make handleReplyBranch verify the last inbound message has a non-NULL sentiment before branching and snooze 1 tick otherwise.
verifyNote: Confirmed: poller.go:196 flips last_direction='in' before the AI call commits classification at poller.go:202, engine.go:117 branches on that flag alone reading stale/NULL sentiment+tags (engine.go:166,261-263; NULL coalesces to neutral→auto-draft), and the wake at poller.go:212 plus DueRuns (sequence/repository.go:223) only match status='active', so a run completed StoppedOnReply never sees the real classification. Caveat: components run sequentially per tick (internalsched/handler.go:65-76, poller registered before engine in main.go:273-276), so the race needs overlapping Cloud Scheduler ticks (no lease exists, ticks can run minutes) — but a crash/5-min timeout between lines 196-202 leaves the stale state permanently, making the next tick misroute deterministically. Fix: prefer the guard variant — handleReplyBranch should require non-NULL sentiment on the last inbound message and snooze one tick otherwise — since reordering alone doesn't cover the crash/timeout case; severity P1 (wrong branch can mark a live lead cold; engagement drafts stay pending_approval so nothing wrong is auto-sent).

title: SetInboundClassification error discarded with '_ =' — silent data loss, not even logged
description: The result of p.conversations.SetInboundClassification is assigned to '_' with no slog. The repository transaction itself is correct (defer Rollback + Commit; the ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE source<>'manual' correctly no-ops on manual rows without erroring), but if Begin/Exec/Commit fails the message stays unclassified and conversation sentiment/tags stay stale — while lines 205-215 still mark the contact replied and wake the active sequence run, which then branches on the stale state (replyPolicy COALESCEs NULL to 'neutral' → auto-draft). Because the AI call already succeeded and the message external_id is recorded, the classification is lost forever with zero observability. The adjacent UpdateLast (196), campaign_contacts (205) and sequence_runs (212) errors are likewise swallowed.
suggestion: At minimum slog.Warn on error with conv/msg IDs. Better: if persisting the classification fails, skip the sequence-run wake (let the next tick retry) or retry the persist; consider folding the replied-marking and wake into the same transaction as SetInboundClassification.
verifyNote: Confirmed: poller.go:202 discards SetInboundClassification's error unlogged (also 196, 205-215), and the external_id idempotency check at poller.go:154-158 means the AI classification is never retried — lost permanently. The stale-branch claim is also accurate: engine.go:261-263 COALESCEs missing sentiment to 'neutral' (Scan error also discarded) and ResolveReplyBranch routes neutral to the positive branch → auto-draft (engine.go:206-212), while the run is still woken at poller.go:212. P1 stands (not P0: trigger is a transient DB failure and drafts are pending_approval, not auto-sent). Fix: fold the replied-mark and run-wake into the SetInboundClassification transaction, or at minimum slog.Warn with conv/msg IDs and skip the sequence-run wake on persist failure.

title: Routing, guidance and lessons consume the lifetime union of conversation tags, not the current reply's tags
description: conversation_tags is keyed (conversation_id, tag) and only out_of_office is ever deleted, so the set is a thread-lifetime union, yet three consumers treat it as 'the current reply': (1) handleReplyBranch routes ResolveIntentRouting over all tags ever (engine.go:166) — a wrong_contact or unsubscribe from an earlier reply permanently overrides the sentiment branch whenever the run is still active (e.g. during an OOO snooze window, a fresh positive reply still routes to notify/suppress); (2) replyguidance.Load pairs the whole-thread tag union with only the latest reply's sentiment bucket, so when drafting a reply to message 3 ('not_interested', negative) it still injects campaign_tag_guidance playbook lines for 'price_requested' answered in message 1, and matches brand_reply_lessons on that mismatched (latest-sentiment x all-time-tags) pair; (3) RememberLesson stores that same union as match_tags, so a lesson learned on a decline is saved tagged 'price_requested' and later leaks into unrelated price conversations. Facet filtering on the union is defensible; routing and guidance on it is not.
suggestion: Add message_id to conversation_tags (tags-per-message), and have ResolveIntentRouting / replyguidance.Load / RememberLesson read only the latest inbound message's tags while facets keep using the per-conversation union. A cheaper interim fix: pass the freshly validated tags from classifyReply through to the engine/guidance instead of re-reading the accumulated table.
verifyNote: Confirmed: conversation_tags PK is (conversation_id, tag) with upsert-only writes (repository.go:288-300, migration 000025:21) and only OOO/manual deletes, so engine.go:166 routes ResolveIntentRouting over the thread-lifetime union (live multi-pass path via OOO snooze at engine.go:122-124,175-185), and loader.go:22-23/47-53/95-105 pair that union with only the latest reply's sentiment for guidance and persist it as lesson match_tags. P1 is right (guidance pollution hits every multi-turn thread; unsubscribe over-trigger fails safe, so not P0). The proposed message_id-per-tag fix is correct, but the 'cheaper interim' pass-through only helps the poller-inline path — the engine consumes tags asynchronously on its tick, so per-message tags are the real fix.

title: Out-of-office and unsubscribe bot replies mark the contact 'Replied' in the group UI and advance the pipeline stage
description: persistIncoming unconditionally sets campaign_contacts.status='replied' (+replied_at) and bumps contacts.pipeline_stage contacted→replied for EVERY inbound — even though the intent tags are already in hand on the previous line (201) and identify out_of_office. The group page's Replied bucket counts cc.status='replied' OR cv.last_direction='in' (group/service.go:425,451), so an OOO auto-responder shows the contact as 'Replied' even though no human ever answered, and the status never reverts (the NOT IN ('replied',...) guard makes it sticky; the engine's OOO branch only snoozes, it never undoes 'replied'). For unsubscribe replies the contact is briefly 'replied' until the engine flips it to 'cold', but the OOO case is permanently wrong and directly conflicts with the 'no_reply cadence runs only while silent' mental model — the user sees Replied, a snoozed run, and later a draft, with zero human engagement.
suggestion: Use the tags computed at line 201: skip the replied-marking and the pipeline-stage bump when tags contain out_of_office (optionally introduce a distinct 'auto_reply' status so the group UI can show 'OOO' instead of 'Replied'), and let the unsubscribe path set 'cold' directly in the poller instead of transiting through 'replied'.
verifyNote: Confirmed: poller.go:201 computes intent tags but lines 205-222 unconditionally set campaign_contacts.status='replied' and bump pipeline_stage contacted->replied for every inbound; the engine's OOO branch (sequence/engine.go:175-185) only consumes the tag and snoozes, never reverting either, and after the 3-day snooze the run falls into the sentiment branch and drafts a reply to the bot (engine.go:117-126, 206-211). Fix suggestion is correct but incomplete: the group Replied bucket (group/service.go:425,451) also matches on `OR cv.last_direction='in'` (set at poller.go:196), so an auto_reply-aware status must also be reflected in that predicate or the OOO contact still counts as Replied.

title: After the 3-day OOO snooze the engine auto-drafts a reply to the bot's auto-response and kills the cadence — it never 'resumes'
description: RouteSnooze deletes the out_of_office tag and bumps the run 3 days, with comments promising 'wait & resume' / 'falls through to the normal branch'. But on resume conv.LastDirection is still 'in' (the OOO reply was the last message), so processOne re-enters handleReplyBranch (line 117), the OOO tag is gone, ResolveIntentRouting returns RouteSentiment, the stored sentiment for the bot message is 'neutral' (prompt mandates score 0.0 for OOO), and the positive/neutral default fires draftReplyForApproval — generating a pending draft that answers 'I am out of office until...' — then CompleteRun(StoppedOnReply). The no_reply cadence can never resume because EvaluateTriggerPure's no_reply trigger requires lastDirection outbound (trigger.go:35), which is unreachable after any inbound. Net effect: an OOO auto-reply ends the entire follow-up sequence and leaves the user a nonsense draft addressed to a bot.
suggestion: On RouteSnooze, record that the last inbound was an auto-reply (e.g. keep a consumed_ooo marker or compare last inbound message tags) and on resume skip the reply branch: re-evaluate the cadence as if the OOO message did not change last_direction (or simply BumpRun until a genuinely new inbound arrives / the step's no_reply window relative to the last outbound elapses).
verifyNote: Confirmed: outreach_sentiment.go:15,41 forces OOO to neutral; nothing resets last_direction during the snooze, so on resume engine.go:117 re-enters handleReplyBranch with the OOO tag already deleted (engine.go:179-181), routes RouteSentiment->positive default->draftReplyForApproval, then CompleteRun(StoppedOnReply) at engine.go:125 — and trigger.go:35 makes no_reply unreachable afterward, so the cadence never resumes, contradicting the comments at engine.go:157,176. P1 (not P0) because the bogus draft is pending_approval, never auto-sent; the suggested fix is correct — mark the OOO inbound consumed (or compare last-inbound vs last-outbound timestamps) and on resume bypass the reply branch, evaluating no_reply relative to the last outbound.

title: LabelForScore and LegacyForScore disagree at score = -0.2: UI shows 'Neutral' while the engine marks the contact cold
description: LabelForScore treats the negative band as score < -0.2 (so exactly -0.2 → 'neutral'), but LegacyForScore treats score <= -0.2 as 'negative'. Both values are computed from the same score in classifyReply and persisted side by side. At exactly -0.2 — a round value LLMs emit often at temperature 0 — the 5-level label shown in the UI/facets is 'Neutral' while the legacy string the reply branch keys off is 'negative', so ResolveReplyBranch takes the negative branch and marks the campaign contact cold. The user sees a Neutral reply whose contact was inexplicably marked cold. The same off-by-inclusion exists at +0.2 (label neutral, legacy positive) but is benign since neutral and positive share the on_positive action.
suggestion: Align the interval edges: LegacyForScore should return negative only for score < -0.2 and positive only for score > 0.2 (mirroring LabelForScore), and add a table test asserting LegacyForScore(s) is consistent with LabelForScore(s) collapsed to 3 buckets for boundary values -0.6, -0.2, 0.2, 0.6.
verifyNote: Confirmed: LabelForScore(-0.2)=neutral (sentiment.go:32-35) but LegacyForScore(-0.2)=negative (sentiment.go:64); both are derived from the same score (poller.go:270-271), the engine branches on the legacy value via last_inbound_sentiment (engine.go:261-263, 236) and defaults to marking the contact cold (engine.go:196-204), while the UI facets show the 5-level label 'neutral' (group/service.go:446-450) — and the +0.2 case is indeed benign since ResolveReplyBranch routes neutral and positive identically. Suggested fix is correct (LegacyForScore: negative only for score < -0.2, positive only for score > 0.2) but must also update the contradictory pinned expectations at sentiment_test.go:35 ({-0.2, negative}) and :39 ({0.2, positive}); note LegacyForScore's own comment "so both stay in sync" (sentiment.go:58) confirms the divergence is unintentional.

title: Inbound dedupe relies on an error-swallowed lookup with no unique index backstop — transient DB error duplicates the message and all side effects
description: Idempotency is solely `existing, _ := p.conversations.FindByExternalID(...)`: on any DB error (not just no-rows) the error is discarded, existing is nil, and the code proceeds to insert. ix_messages_external is a plain CREATE INDEX, not UNIQUE, so nothing at the DB level prevents the duplicate. Because pollOne deliberately re-fetches a 2-minute overlap window every poll (line 106), recently seen messages are re-checked on every cycle; a transient error during that check yields a duplicate inbound message row, a second AI classification (and cost), a second sequence-run wake, and potentially a second pending draft.
suggestion: Distinguish ErrNotFound from real errors in persistIncoming (on real error: skip the message this tick and let the overlap retry), and add a partial unique index: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON messages(external_id) WHERE external_id IS NOT NULL, treating the conflict as 'already seen'.
verifyNote: Confirmed: poller.go:155 discards the error from FindByExternalID, which returns domain.ErrNotFound vs real errors (repository.go:539-544); CreateMessage is a plain INSERT with no ON CONFLICT (repository.go:462-471) and ix_messages_external is non-unique (migrations/000009:47, no later migration adds uniqueness), so a transient DB error during the 2-min-overlap re-check (poller.go:106) duplicates the row plus AI classification, sequence wake, and SSE side effects. P2 is the honest severity (needs a transient error coinciding with the overlap window); the suggested fix is correct — distinguish ErrNotFound and add the partial unique index, noting external_id is the RFC Message-ID header (gmail.go:273) so a global unique index matches existing FindByExternalID semantics, though scoping it to (conversation_id, external_id) would be safer.

title: score == 0 is used as a 'model omitted score' sentinel, conflating genuine 0.0 with missing and letting the legacy string override it
description: OutreachSentimentResult.Score is a plain float64, so an absent "score" key and an explicit "score": 0.0 both unmarshal to 0. The back-compat heuristic then trusts the legacy field: a reply the model genuinely scored 0.0 (the prompt explicitly anchors 0.0 = neutral/auto-reply/bare question) but inconsistently labeled sentiment:"positive" or "negative" gets rewritten to ±0.5, flipping the stored label to positive/negative and (for negative) the engine branch to mark-cold. The same pattern is duplicated in simulation/aicalls.go:85. clampScore itself is fine for the reachable domain (encoding/json cannot produce NaN/Inf, and out-of-range literals fail unmarshal into the error path).
suggestion: Change Score to *float64 (or pre-scan the raw JSON for the "score" key) so 'missing' is detectable; apply ScoreForLegacy only when the key is truly absent, and prefer the explicit score when both are present.
verifyNote: Confirmed: Score is a plain float64 (outreach_sentiment.go:68) so missing and explicit 0.0 collapse; poller.go:267-268 (and the duplicate in simulation/aicalls.go:85-87) then rewrite a genuine 0.0 to ±0.5 via ScoreForLegacy, and a "negative" legacy flows through LegacyForScore (sentiment.go:62-65) into ResolveReplyBranch's default mark-cold path (engine.go:196-204, 245). P2 is right since the trigger needs a self-contradictory model output (score 0.0 + non-neutral sentiment); the *float64 fix is correct and should be applied to both call sites.

title: AI cache key has no tenant scoping and cache hits bypass the request log
description: CacheKey = sha256(provider|model|system|prompt|temperature) with no user/tenant component, so the 24h outreach_sentiment entries are shared across all users. Practical cross-user confidentiality leakage is nil today — a hit requires the byte-identical prompt, meaning the other tenant already holds the same email content — but the design is fragile (any future key change that drops full-prompt hashing, or a prompt built from partial content, becomes a real leak), and classification output containing a quoted line of customer email ('reason') sits in shared Redis for 24h. The concrete present-day defect is in router.Complete: a cache hit returns at line 98 before the slog and before r.logFunc, so cached classifications produce no ai_request_logs row — per-user cost/usage attribution silently undercounts, and the user whose ctx userID rode the hit is never recorded. Note also the hit rate for this task is near zero by construction (external_id idempotency means each message classifies once; only byte-identical bot bodies ever hit).
suggestion: Invoke logFunc on cache hits too (AIResult already carries CacheHit=true, with zero cost), and either add the tenant ID to CacheKey for user-scoped tasks or document the invariant that keys must always hash the complete prompt.
verifyNote: Confirmed: cache.go:54-58 hashes no tenant component, and router.go:95-98 returns cached results before the logFunc call at router.go:125-129, so cache hits never write ai_request_logs — despite the pipeline being wired for it (cache.go:37 sets CacheHit=true, main.go:141 and ailog/repository.go:25 persist a cache_hit column that can therefore never be true). Description is accurate including the near-zero hit rate (poller.go:151-155 external_id idempotency) and the 'reason' field quoting customer email (prompts/outreach_sentiment.go:49); note the logging bypass also affects classification/scoring/excel_mapping/outreach_draft/reply call sites with nonzero TTLs, but since hits cost $0 it only undercounts attribution metrics — P2 stands. Fix as suggested: call logFunc on the hit path before router.go:97 and add tenant ID to CacheKey for user-scoped tasks (or document the full-prompt-hash invariant).

title: Cadence mark_cold globally suppresses the contact as if they legally unsubscribed
description: fireAction's mark_cold calls contacts.MarkUnsubscribed(ctx, conv.ContactID, "sequence_marked_cold"), which sets contacts.unsubscribed_at (contact/repository.go:429-437). unsubscribed_at is exactly what compliance.IsSuppressed gates (compliance/unsubscribe.go:101-103), and the campaign scheduler skips every suppressed contact in ALL future campaigns (campaign/scheduler.go:60-63, skip reason 'contact unsubscribed'). So a contact who merely never answered one cadence is permanently blocked from all future outreach, indistinguishable from a CAN-SPAM opt-out. Worse, MarkUnsubscribed uses COALESCE on both unsubscribed_at and unsubscribe_reason, so if the contact later genuinely unsubscribes (one-click or reply keyword), the audit trail still reads 'sequence_marked_cold' with the cadence-exhaustion timestamp — corrupted compliance data. This is inconsistent with handleReplyBranch's negative path (engine.go:201-203) which only sets campaign_contacts.status='cold' (campaign-scoped), and with the Simulation Lab (simulation/service.go:315-317) which presents mark_cold as 'No reply after the cadence — marked cold', i.e. campaign-scoped — so production does something materially harsher than what the Lab that 'mirrors production' tells the user.
suggestion: In fireAction's mark_cold, mirror the negative-reply path: UPDATE campaign_contacts SET status='cold' WHERE conversation_id=$1 (and optionally move pipeline_stage), and reserve contacts.MarkUnsubscribed strictly for compliance events (one-click, reply keyword, unsubscribe intent). If a global 'do not re-prospect' flag is wanted, add a separate contacts column rather than overloading unsubscribed_at.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:371-372 routes the cadence mark_cold action to contacts.MarkUnsubscribed("sequence_marked_cold"), which sets contacts.unsubscribed_at (contact/repository.go:429-438); compliance.IsSuppressed (unsubscribe.go:101-103) then makes campaign/scheduler.go:61-63 skip the contact in ALL future campaigns with no resubscribe path anywhere in the backend, and the COALESCE on unsubscribe_reason means a later genuine opt-out (one_click, reply_keyword, reply_intent_unsubscribe) keeps the bogus "sequence_marked_cold" audit record. The suggested fix is correct — mirror the negative-reply path (engine.go:200-203, UPDATE campaign_contacts SET status='cold' WHERE conversation_id=$1) and reserve MarkUnsubscribed for compliance events, matching the domain comment (outreach.go:320) and Simulation Lab semantics (simulation/service.go:315-317).

title: Reply auto-draft and the approve-and-send path never re-check suppression
description: compliance/unsubscribe.go:99-100 states senders MUST call IsSuppressed immediately before dispatching any campaign or sequence message. The cadence path honors this (engine.go:416 actionSendMessage; campaign/scheduler.go:61) but two paths do not: (1) draftReplyForApproval (engine.go:287-291) loads the contact and drafts without an IsSuppressed check, so an already-unsubscribed contact who replies (or an unsubscribe reply whose intent tag was dropped by the <0.5 confidence floor) gets a pending AI draft; (2) conversation SendMessage — the endpoint that sends an approved pending_approval draft — performs no suppression check at all before ch.Send (it only checks PrimaryEmail at line 198). Net effect: a contact who used the one-click unsubscribe link can still be emailed via approve-and-send, with the user never warned. The footer/unsubscribe URL added on the auto-send path (engine.go:497-501) is also absent here.
suggestion: Add compliance.IsSuppressed(c) checks: in draftReplyForApproval return early (or create a notify task: 'replied but is unsubscribed') instead of drafting, and in conversation Service.SendMessage refuse to send to a suppressed contact (HTTP 409 with the unsubscribe reason) unless the user explicitly overrides.
verifyNote: Confirmed: conversation/service.go SendMessage (lines 139-304) imports no compliance package and only checks PrimaryEmail (line 198) before ch.Send (line 237), yet it is the only dispatch path for sequence-created pending_approval drafts (engine.go:344/482, frontend conversation-thread.tsx:107) — violating the contract at compliance/unsubscribe.go:99-100 that the gated paths (engine.go:416, scheduler.go:61) honor; draftReplyForApproval (engine.go:288-291) likewise drafts without an IsSuppressed check, and the poller's <0.5 confidence floor (poller.go:278) can drop the unsubscribe intent tag as described. P1 (not P0) because every leak requires an explicit human approve-and-send click and all auto-send paths are gated; the suggested fix (409 on suppressed in SendMessage, early-return/notify-task in draftReplyForApproval) is correct — also add the compliance footer on this path.

title: OOO snooze resumes by auto-drafting a reply to the out-of-office auto-responder
description: RouteSnooze deletes the out_of_office tag and BumpRuns +3d, with the comment 'don't draft a reply to a bot' (engine.go:177). But on resume the conversation's last_direction is still 'in' (nothing changed it), so processOne re-enters handleReplyBranch (engine.go:117); the OOO tag is gone, so ResolveIntentRouting returns RouteSentiment; replyPolicy reads conversations.last_inbound_sentiment, which is still the OOO reply's classification (typically neutral), so the default branch calls draftReplyForApproval. The draft prompt runs in Mode 'reply' whose instruction is literally 'Draft a reply to the most recent inbound message' (prompts/outreach_reply.go:136), and ListMessages puts the OOO auto-reply as the final THEM message in ConversationText — so 3 days later the system does exactly what the comment says it avoids: it drafts a reply addressed at the bot's 'I'm out of office until …' text. The fixed 3-day window also ignores any return date in the OOO body. The simulation (simulation/service.go:234-241) faithfully mirrors this, so the Lab shows the same odd draft.
suggestion: On resume, don't fall into the reply branch against the OOO message: record the snooze on the run (e.g. a resume_mode column or in-band marker) and on wake either (a) draft with Mode 'followup' excluding the OOO message from ConversationText, or (b) re-enter the no_reply cadence by treating the OOO inbound as non-engagement (e.g. skip inbound messages tagged out_of_office when computing last_direction for the branch).
verifyNote: Confirmed end to end: RouteSnooze deletes the OOO tag and only bumps next_run_at (engine.go:175-185, repository.go:251), leaving last_direction='in' (set at poller.go:196), so on resume processOne:117 re-enters handleReplyBranch; with the tag gone ResolveIntentRouting→RouteSentiment, and the OOO reply's stored sentiment is neutral (score 0.0 per outreach_sentiment.go:41, LegacyForScore at sentiment.go:60-68), so the default OnPositiveAutoDraftReply path calls draftReplyForApproval with Mode 'reply' ('Draft a reply to the most recent inbound message', outreach_reply.go:136) over a ConversationText ending with the OOO auto-reply (it has Status=sent, poller.go:187, not filtered at engine.go:300) — exactly contradicting the 'don't draft a reply to a bot' comment; simulation/service.go:234-241 mirrors it. P1 not P0: the draft is pending_approval and never auto-sent, so impact is an odd human-reviewed draft, not a bad send. The suggested fix is sound, with one caveat: since the tag is deleted on snooze, option (b) needs the snooze recorded on the run (resume_mode/snoozed_until) or the tag kept; otherwise option (a) — resume with Mode 'followup' excluding the OOO message — is the simpler change.

title: Reply routing (including unsubscribe-intent suppression) only exists while a sequence run is active
description: handleReplyBranch is only reachable from processOne, i.e. from a due, status='active' sequence_run; the poller wake also targets only active runs (poller/poller.go:212-215). Once a run ends — 'completed' after the last cadence step, or 'stopped_on_reply' after the first handled reply — subsequent inbound replies are classified and tagged but never routed: no auto-draft, no wrong_contact notify, and critically no unsubscribe-intent suppression (only the conservative keyword scan at poller.go:226-230 remains as a backstop). A buyer who replies on day 5 gets an auto-draft; the same reply on day 20 (after the cadence completed) silently does nothing, which contradicts the advertised 'every inbound reply is reacted to' behavior. Additionally, processOne fetches the step BEFORE the reply check (engine.go:95-102): if current_step exceeds the step list (e.g. steps edited down while a run was live), the run completes 'completed' even when an unhandled inbound reply is pending, skipping routing entirely.
suggestion: Move intent routing out of the run lifecycle: have the poller (or a small reply-router Tickable) invoke the intent/sentiment branch for every newly classified inbound on a campaign conversation regardless of run state — at minimum always honor RouteSuppress. In processOne, perform the LastDirection==inbound check before the GetStep call so a pending reply is routed even when the step is gone.
verifyNote: Confirmed: handleReplyBranch is reachable only via processOne on a due active run (engine.go:118; repository.go:223 DueRuns filters status='active'; poller.go:212-215 wakes only active runs), so post-run inbound replies are classified+tagged (poller.go:201-202) but never auto-drafted, notified, or intent-suppressed — only the 7-keyword LooksLikeOptOut backstop (poller.go:226-230, compliance/unsubscribe.go:113-120) remains; and engine.go:95-102 completes a run on GetStep ErrNotFound before the inbound check at line 117, skipping routing of a pending reply. P1 stands (visible behavioral asymmetry plus a partially-backstopped compliance gap), not P0 since IsSuppressed gates all sends (engine.go:416) and the one-click unsubscribe works regardless; the "advertised behavior" framing is slightly overstated (no such doc promise; replies still surface as unread via SSE). The suggested fix is correct — route intents (at minimum RouteSuppress) from the poller for every classified inbound regardless of run state, and move the LastDirection check before GetStep in processOne.

title: loadConvTags swallows query errors, so an unsubscribe reply can be auto-drafted with no retry possible
description: loadConvTags returns nil on pool.Query error and silently skips rows whose Scan fails. ResolveIntentRouting(nil) = RouteSentiment, so a transient DB error while handling an unsubscribe reply routes it to the sentiment branch: a pending AI draft is created for someone who asked to stop, contacts.MarkUnsubscribed is never called, and — the part that makes this unrecoverable — processOne then calls CompleteRun(stopped_on_reply), so the run never re-evaluates; the misroute is permanent, not retried next tick. Combined with the missing suppression check in SendMessage (separate finding), the user can approve and send that draft. Likelihood is low (DB flake on a single query) but every other error in processOne correctly aborts and retries via the still-active run; this is the one error path that silently commits a wrong, terminal decision on the compliance-critical branch.
suggestion: Change loadConvTags to return ([]string, error) and propagate the error from handleReplyBranch so processOne returns it — the run stays active and is retried next tick, matching how every other failure in this path behaves.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:217-219 returns nil on Query error (and never checks rows.Err()), trigger.go:82-83 maps nil tags to RouteSentiment, and engine.go:125 + repository.go:223/259 make the stopped_on_reply completion terminal — uniquely among processOne error paths, which all return and retry. Mitigation note: poller.go:226-230 already suppresses keyword-obvious opt-outs at ingestion, so only AI-tagged non-keyword unsubscribes are exposed, supporting P1 not P0. Fix is correct (return ([]string, error), propagate through handleReplyBranch); also propagate Scan errors and check rows.Err(), since a silently skipped unsubscribe row misroutes the same way.

title: DueRuns has no row locking and ticks have no overlap guard — concurrent ticks double-process runs (duplicate drafts / duplicate auto-sent emails)
description: DueRuns is a plain SELECT (no FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, no claimed_at/lease), and a run's next_run_at/status is only updated AFTER the action fires — which includes one or two AI completions and a Gmail send per run (engine.go:139-153). The tick endpoint is plain HTTP fan-out with no mutex or advisory lock (internalsched/handler.go:61-76), and the deployment is Cloud Run where Cloud Scheduler retries, manual curl, or a second instance can overlap a slow tick (up to 100 runs x multi-second AI calls easily exceeds a 1-minute tick interval; each component is allowed 5 minutes). Two overlapping ticks both read the same due run and both fire it: duplicate pending_approval drafts in the inbox, or — on the auto_send path — the same follow-up email actually sent twice to the buyer.
suggestion: Either add SKIP LOCKED claiming (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED inside a transaction that immediately bumps next_run_at as a claim) or guard the whole tick with pg_try_advisory_lock / an in-process TryLock that returns 200 'tick already running'.
verifyNote: Confirmed: DueRuns is an unlocked SELECT (repository.go:220-226) and the run is only advanced after fireAction completes its AI calls + Gmail send (engine.go:139-153, 511), while the tick handler has no mutex/advisory lock and allows 5 min per component vs a 1-minute scheduler cadence (internalsched/handler.go:61-76); no unique index on messages dedupes the result (migrations/000009). Overlapping ticks (scheduler retry, manual curl per main.go:268-269, or multi-instance Cloud Run) therefore double-fire due runs — duplicate pending drafts or a duplicate auto-sent email. P1 is honest (race-conditional, not deterministic). Best fix: claim rows atomically with UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING, which also covers multi-instance.

title: Engine deletes the out_of_office tag outright — destroys the UI facet/audit record and clobbers manual tags
description: RouteSnooze runs DELETE FROM conversation_tags WHERE conversation_id=$1 AND tag='out_of_office' with no source filter. conversation_tags doubles as the classification record consumed by the group page faceted filter and facet counts (group/service.go:400, 468), conversation tag chips (conversation/repository.go:166, 226-244), and brand-lesson tag-overlap matching (replyguidance/loader.go:68). After the engine consumes the tag, the conversation silently disappears from the out_of_office facet even though the user saw the OOO reply land, and the eventual resume draft loads guidance that no longer matches out_of_office lessons. The delete also removes source='manual' rows, contradicting the system's own rule that manual tags must not be clobbered by automation (SetInboundClassification guards with WHERE source <> 'manual', conversation/repository.go:293-295; AddManualTag promotes to protect it, 246-257).
suggestion: Don't use the classification record as routing state: persist the snooze on the run itself (e.g. sequence_runs.snoozed_for='out_of_office' or a handled_tags marker keyed by message id) and leave conversation_tags intact; at minimum restrict the DELETE to source='ai'.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:179-182 deletes the out_of_office tag with no source filter and no restore path, removing the conversation from the group facet filter/counts (group/service.go:400, 468), tag chips (conversation/repository.go:166, 226-244), and lesson matching (replyguidance/loader.go:68); it also deletes source='manual' rows, contradicting the manual-protection invariant in SetInboundClassification (repository.go:293-295) and AddManualTag (246-257), and users can set out_of_office manually via the AddTag endpoint (handler.go:58-80). Fix: persist snooze state on the run (suggestion's primary option) — note the fallback "DELETE ... AND source='ai'" alone would leave manual OOO tags re-triggering RouteSnooze indefinitely since loadConvTags (engine.go:216) reads tags regardless of source, so the routing read must also be made snooze-aware.

title: ReplaceSteps silently rewrites every trigger to no_reply; dead conditional; frontend type still advertises 4 triggers
description: The coercion `trigger := st.Trigger; if trigger != domain.SequenceTriggerNoReply { trigger = no_reply }` is a constant assignment dressed as a conditional. The API accepts any trigger value ('always', 'any_reply', 'positive_reply') and persists something else without error or warning; normalizeSteps' comment claims it 'validates trigger/action' (service.go:104) but only defaults empties. The frontend type still exports SequenceTrigger = "no_reply" | "any_reply" | "positive_reply" | "always" (frontend/src/lib/types/outreach.ts:219), so a client can legally send a value that comes back mutated in the ListSteps response. Per-step reply triggers being removed is the accepted trade-off; the knock-on issues are the silent mutation of user input and the contract drift. Note also rows written before this coercion existed are untouched — a legacy 'always' step would fire immediately via EvaluateTriggerPure (trigger.go:30-31) ignoring its wait, since only ReplaceSteps coerces.
suggestion: Reject unsupported triggers with a 400 in normalizeSteps (or accept-and-coerce but document it and narrow the frontend type to "no_reply"), replace the dead conditional with a direct assignment plus comment, and add a one-off migration coercing legacy sequence_steps rows so stored data matches the invariant.
verifyNote: Confirmed: repository.go:138-141 is a constant assignment dressed as a conditional that silently coerces any client-sent trigger to no_reply; normalizeSteps (service.go:104) claims validation but only defaults empties, and frontend types/outreach.ts:219 still advertises 4 triggers. The legacy-rows premise is real (git show fc2635e: ReplaceSteps persisted st.Trigger verbatim and the old sequence-step-editor offered any_reply/positive_reply; no migration coerces sequence_steps.trigger), though one detail is overstated — a legacy 'always' step would not skip its wait, since next_run_at scheduling (engine.go:152, service.go:85) already encodes wait_days; it only bypasses the no-reply gate. Fix as suggested: reject (400) or document the coercion and narrow the frontend type to "no_reply", replace the dead conditional with a direct assignment, and add a one-off UPDATE migration on sequence_steps.trigger.

title: StartRun's documented idempotency is broken: duplicate start returns ErrNotFound, and a finished run permanently blocks restart
description: StartRun does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (sequence_id, conversation_id) DO NOTHING and then GetRun(id) with the freshly generated id. On conflict no row was inserted, so GetRun returns domain.ErrNotFound — the caller gets an error, not the existing run, contradicting StartRunForConversation's docstring 'Idempotent — calling twice... leaves the existing run alone' (service.go:74-76). The campaign scheduler treats it as non-fatal but logs a spurious 'start sequence run failed' warning on every re-send to an existing conversation (campaign/scheduler.go:203-208). Because uq_sequence_run_conv is unconditional (migrations/000013_sequences.up.sql:42) and DO NOTHING never revives a row, once a run is completed/stopped_on_reply that sequence can never be restarted for that conversation through this path — it silently no-ops with an error.
suggestion: On conflict, SELECT the existing row and return it (e.g. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET updated_at=now() RETURNING id, or a follow-up SELECT by (sequence_id, conversation_id)); decide explicitly whether restart-after-completion should reactivate the run and implement that as a deliberate UPDATE.
verifyNote: Confirmed: repository.go:191-203 does ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then GetRun with the fresh uuid, so a duplicate start returns domain.ErrNotFound (repository.go:211-213), contradicting the idempotency docstring at service.go:73-75; uq_sequence_run_conv (000013_sequences.up.sql:42) is unconditional so a completed/stopped run permanently blocks the pair. However the "warning on every re-send" claim is overstated — the sole caller (campaign/scheduler.go:203-208) only fires on first send of a freshly created conversation (drafter.go:166-178 never reuses conversations; RetryFailed only retries rows that failed before StartCampaignRun), so this is a latent contract bug, not one currently triggering in production. P2 is the right severity; the suggested ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING fix (or follow-up SELECT by (sequence_id, conversation_id)) is the correct repair.

title: draftReplyForApproval silently returns nil when the contact is missing or has no email — run completes 'handled' with no draft and no notification
description: `if err != nil || c == nil || c.PrimaryEmail == nil || *c.PrimaryEmail == "" { return err }` returns nil when the lookup succeeded but the contact is nil or has no primary email. processOne then runs CompleteRun(stopped_on_reply): a positive/neutral buyer reply produces no draft, no task, and the run is terminally closed, so the lead silently falls through the cracks. This is the concrete answer to 'any path that should NOT complete the run but does'. The cadence twin at engine.go:420-422 has the same shape (no email -> return nil) which causes processOne to ADVANCE to the next step as if the send fired.
suggestion: When the contact can't be drafted to, surface it instead of returning nil: create a notify task ('replied but contact has no email') or return a typed error so the run stays active/errored rather than completing as handled; same treatment for the actionSendMessage skip.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:288-291 returns nil for a no-email contact, so processOne:125 runs CompleteRun(stopped_on_reply) with no draft and no task; the twin at engine.go:420-422 returns nil and processOne:144-153 advances the step as if sent. Minor correction: the "contact missing" case is not silent — contact/repository.go:262-263 returns ErrNotFound so the run errors (c==nil is dead code); only the no-email case swallows. Fix direction is right and matches existing precedent (campaign drafter.go:60/scheduler.go:64 record explicit "no email" skips); additionally, the reply-path guard could just drop the email check since drafting a pending_approval message never uses the address.

title: notifyReply silently no-ops when tasks is nil, while fireAction's notify_user would nil-panic — inconsistent guards
description: notifyReply returns nil when e.tasks == nil, so a wrong_contact or notify-policy reply would 'succeed' with no task created and processOne would CompleteRun(stopped_on_reply) — the user is never told, and the signal is unrecoverable. Meanwhile fireAction's notify_user case (engine.go:394) calls e.tasks.CreateTask with no nil guard at all, which would panic on a nil interface. In production main.go always wires crmRepo (cmd/server/main.go:236-240), so today this is latent, but the two code paths embody opposite assumptions about the same field; whichever assumption is wrong, one path fails silently and the other crashes the tick.
suggestion: Make the contract explicit: either require TaskNotifier in NewEngine (panic at construction if nil) and drop the notifyReply guard, or guard both paths and return an error (not nil) when the notifier is absent so the run is retried/surfaced instead of completing as handled.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:269-271 silently returns nil when e.tasks==nil (and processOne:122-125 then CompleteRun(stopped_on_reply), dropping the reply signal), while engine.go:394 calls e.tasks.CreateTask with no guard and would nil-panic — opposite assumptions about the same field. Latent only: main.go:236-240 is the sole NewEngine call site and always wires crmRepo, so P2 smell is the honest severity. Fix: validate non-nil TaskNotifier in NewEngine and drop the dead guard in notifyReply (preferred over guarding both paths, since only one caller exists).

title: AI intent tags accumulate per conversation forever, so routing and lesson-matching use stale tags from earlier replies
description: SetInboundClassification upserts the new reply's tags but never removes AI tags from prior replies, and the engine's loadConvTags (engine.go:216-230) reads ALL conversation_tags rows, not the latest message's tags. Routing therefore reacts to the union of every intent ever seen: e.g. a reply once tagged wrong_contact keeps that tag forever, so if the user later restarts a sequence (or a second sequence is attached to the same conversation), a genuinely positive new reply is routed to RouteNotify ('Wrong contact — needs your attention') instead of auto-draft; replyguidance.Load similarly matches brand lessons against the accumulated tag set, injecting guidance written for intents the current reply doesn't have. The sentiment columns are correctly last-reply-scoped (last_inbound_sentiment), making the conversation-lifetime tag scope an inconsistency between the two halves of the same classification.
suggestion: Scope routing to the triggering reply: store tags per message (message_id column on conversation_tags, or a messages.intent_tags array) and have handleReplyBranch/replyguidance load the latest inbound message's tags, keeping the conversation-level union only for the group-page facets.
verifyNote: Confirmed: AI tags only accumulate — SetInboundClassification upserts without clearing prior AI tags (repository.go:288-300; only deletions are manual RemoveTag at :261 and the engine's OOO-consumption at engine.go:179-183), while loadConvTags (engine.go:217) and replyguidance.convTags (loader.go:68) read the lifetime union, contradicting loader.go:2-4/44-46's own "keyed off the inbound reply's intent tags" contract; sentiment is meanwhile last-reply-scoped (repository.go:280-287). However the finding's headline scenario is overstated: no API restarts a sequence on an existing conversation (sequence/handler.go has no run endpoint) and campaigns pre-create fresh conversations (drafter.go:134-166), so cross-sequence wrong_contact misrouting is unreachable; the real exposure is a same-run case (reply tagged OOO+wrong_contact → snooze consumes only OOO → later positive reply routes to Notify) plus stale-tag guidance/lesson pollution on any multi-turn thread. P2 stands. The suggested fix is right: store tags per message (message_id on conversation_tags) and have handleReplyBranch/replyguidance load only the latest inbound message's tags, keeping the conversation-level union for group-page facets.

title: Group email list 500s once any email is sent: timestamptz scanned into *string
description: Emails() selects cv.last_message_at (TIMESTAMPTZ per migration 000009) and scans it into `var lastAt *string`. pgx v5.9.1 with the default query exec mode (db.NewPool sets no override, no default_query_exec_mode in any DSN in the repo) requests binary format for timestamptz and cannot scan it into *string. Verified empirically against the project's local DB with the exact pgx version: `cannot scan timestamptz (OID 1184) in binary format into **string`. NULL scans succeed, so the endpoint works on a fresh group and breaks permanently the moment the first send/reply sets last_message_at (poller.UpdateLast / UpdateContactSent) — every row in GET /outreach/groups/{id}/emails then fails with 'scan group email', taking down the whole group email pane. ListInbox correctly scans the same column into *time.Time (domain.Conversation.LastMessageAt), confirming the inconsistency.
suggestion: Scan into *time.Time and format to RFC3339 when populating GroupEmail.LastMessageAt (matching ListInbox), or cast in SQL: `cv.last_message_at::text` (or to_char(...)). Add a test that exercises Emails() with a non-NULL last_message_at row.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:376-383 scans TIMESTAMPTZ cv.last_message_at (migrations/000009:15) into *string; pool uses pgx v5.9.1 default exec mode with no override (db/postgres.go:12-36, config.go:100-112), and I reproduced the exact failure against the project's local DB ("cannot scan timestamptz (OID 1184) in binary format into **string" for non-NULL, success for NULL), so GET /outreach/groups/{id}/emails 500s permanently once UpdateLast (conversation/repository.go:205) sets the timestamp. Fix as suggested: scan into *time.Time and format RFC3339, matching ListInbox (domain/outreach.go:133).

title: 'Replied' status facet includes contacts already marked cold — chips double-count
description: statusPredicate('replied') = (cc.status='replied' OR cv.last_direction='in'). The negative reply branch (sequence/engine.go:173,202) sets cc.status='cold' on contacts whose last message is inbound (last_direction='in'), so every auto-cold-marked contact still matches the replied predicate via the OR arm. facetCounts uses the identical FILTER expressions (lines 451-453), so the chip counts match the filtered lists (I verified counts and filters use the same joins/predicates — no chip-says-3-list-shows-2 mismatch), but the same row is counted in BOTH the Replied and Cold chips: status chips sum to more than the member count, and clicking 'Replied' surfaces contacts the system already wrote off as cold. The same row also appears under negative/very_negative sentiment chips, which is fine (different dimension), but replied-vs-cold are presented as one mutually exclusive status dimension in the UI.
suggestion: Exclude terminal statuses from the OR arm: `(cc.status = 'replied' OR (cv.last_direction = 'in' AND cc.status NOT IN ('cold','skipped','failed')))` in both statusPredicate and the facetCounts FILTER — or drop the last_direction arm entirely, since the poller already sets cc.status='replied' on every first inbound (poller.go:205-209).
verifyNote: Confirmed: statusPredicate('replied') at group/service.go:424-425 (and identical FILTER at :451) matches any cv.last_direction='in' row, while sequence/engine.go:201-203 and :172-174 set cc.status='cold' on contacts whose last message is inbound (poller.go:196 sets last_direction='in' via repository.go:206-211, and the cold branch sends nothing outbound) — so the same row counts in both Replied and Cold chips, which facet-filter-bar.tsx:6-10 presents as one status dimension. The suggested fix is correct; prefer the variant that keeps the OR arm but adds `AND cc.status NOT IN ('cold','skipped','failed')` (in both service.go:425 and :451) over dropping it, since the poller's status='replied' UPDATE (poller.go:205-209) is best-effort with errors discarded.

title: SavePlaybook silently drops blank/invalid rows; UI then deletes the user's just-added rule with a success message
description: SavePlaybook skips any entry with an unknown tag or whitespace-only instruction with `continue` — no error, no indication. The frontend (groups/[groupId]/page.tsx savePlaybook) replaces editor state with the response: `setPlaybook(res.playbook)` and shows 'Playbook saved'. PlaybookEditor's 'Add rule' button creates a row with instruction:"" — if the user saves before filling it in (or leaves any rule blank), the row vanishes from the editor under a success toast. The delete-then-insert transaction itself is fine for concurrent GetPlaybook readers (MVCC: they see either the old or new full set, never the empty intermediate state), so the only user-facing problem is the silent drop.
suggestion: Return 400 (or a `dropped: [...]` field in the 200 response) when entries are filtered out, and/or have the frontend validate non-empty instructions before submit instead of blindly adopting the server response.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:231-232 silently `continue`s past invalid-tag/blank-instruction entries, handler.go:210-216 returns 200 with the filtered playbook, page.tsx:122-124 does setPlaybook(res.playbook) + "Playbook saved", and playbook-editor.tsx:72 adds rows with instruction:"" — so a just-added blank rule vanishes under a success message. Low-end P1 (UI's tag select means only whitespace-only instructions can drop, so no substantive content is lost); fix as suggested — frontend-validate non-empty instructions before submit (cheapest) and/or have the server 400 or report dropped entries instead of silently filtering.

title: Inbox snippet and message count include unsent AI drafts
description: ListInbox's snippet subquery (`SELECT substring(...) FROM messages m WHERE m.conversation_id = c.id ORDER BY m.created_at DESC LIMIT 1`) and msg_count subquery have no status filter, so a status='pending_approval' auto-drafted reply (created by the reply branch immediately after an inbound message) becomes the inbox row's preview text — the user sees their own unsent draft presented as the latest message in the thread, and the count includes messages that were never sent. The same file's recentNonDraftMessages (line 423) deliberately excludes 'draft'/'pending_approval', confirming drafts are not meant to read as conversation content. The total-count vs page-query consistency is otherwise fine (both filter user_id + unread + status<>'paused'; the INNER JOINs cannot drop rows since conversations.contact_id and contacts.business_id are NOT NULL with cascading deletes), and the per-row correlated subselects (tags ARRAY, snippet, count) are each PK/index lookups — acceptable at page size 25.
suggestion: Add `AND m.status NOT IN ('draft','pending_approval')` to both the snippet and msg_count subselects (or surface a separate has_pending_draft flag if the UI wants to show draft presence explicitly).
verifyNote: Confirmed: repository.go:168-171 has no status filter while engine.go:336-345 (auto_draft_reply default, engine.go:210) inserts a pending_approval message right after an inbound reply with created_at DEFAULT now(), so the draft would win the ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 snippet; the suggested NOT IN ('draft','pending_approval') fix on both subselects is correct. Downgraded to P2 because the field is never rendered: /outreach redirects to /outreach/groups (frontend app/(dashboard)/outreach/page.tsx), listConversations (lib/api/outreach.ts:120) and ConversationListItem have zero callers/importers, and the live group inbox uses group/service.go:347-365 which selects no snippet — so no user currently sees the draft.

title: Unknown status facet values silently widen results instead of narrowing
description: statusPredicate whitelists four keys and returns "" for anything else; buildFacetWhere drops empty predicates, and if every supplied status value is unknown the entire status clause disappears — `?status=bounced` returns the FULL unfiltered list. This is inconsistent with the sentiment and tag facets, where an unknown value is parameterized as-is and correctly matches zero rows. A stale bookmark or client bug filtering on a removed status key shows everything while the UI implies a filter is active.
suggestion: Treat unknown status keys as FALSE (e.g. append a literal 'FALSE' predicate) or reject them with 400 in the handler, mirroring how unknown sentiment/tag values yield empty results.
verifyNote: Confirmed: statusPredicate returns "" for unknown keys (service.go:432-433) and buildFacetWhere appends the status clause only if len(preds)>0 (service.go:409-411), so ?status=bounced yields a fully unfiltered list, unlike sentiment/tags which parameterize raw values and match zero rows (service.go:393-401); handler.go:140-145 does no validation. However, facets are React useState (not URL-persisted) and the UI only emits the four whitelisted keys, so the "stale bookmark" path doesn't exist today — P2 stands. Fix: return 400 from the handler for unknown status keys (preferred), or append a literal FALSE predicate to mirror sentiment/tag behavior.

title: facet_counts merges three facet dimensions into one flat key namespace
description: GroupDetail.FacetCounts is a single map[string]int keyed by sentiment label, status key, AND intent tag; the tag GROUP BY loop writes `out[tag] = n` into the same map that holds 'replied'/'cold'/'negative' etc. Today the three vocabularies are disjoint (verified: the 16 IntentVocabulary tags in domain/intent.go share no value with the 4 status keys or 5 sentiment labels), but adding a tag whose name collides with a status/sentiment key would silently overwrite that chip's count with no compile-time or runtime signal. The frontend indexes the same flat map for all three chip rows (facet-filter-bar.tsx counts[...]).
suggestion: Namespace the payload — e.g. `facet_counts: {sentiment: {...}, status: {...}, tags: {...}}` — or at minimum prefix tag keys (`tag:price_requested`) and add a unit test asserting the three key sets stay disjoint.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:441-484 writes 5 sentiment keys, 4 status keys, and `out[tag] = n` into one flat map (field at service.go:70), and facet-filter-bar.tsx:77,93,110 indexes that same flat record for all three chip rows; the 16 tags in domain/intent.go:38-45 are verified disjoint from the 9 status/sentiment keys today, so this is a latent collision smell, not a live bug — P2 stands. The tag GROUP BY (service.go:467-473) also lacks a vocabulary filter, so the namespaced-payload fix ({sentiment, status, tags}) is the right one, with the disjointness unit test as a cheaper fallback.

title: SavePlaybook handler ignores re-fetch error and can return playbook:null, crashing the editor
description: After a successful save, the handler does `entries, _ := h.svc.GetPlaybook(...)` and returns 200 with whatever came back. On a transient DB error entries is nil, so the response is {"playbook": null}. The frontend savePlaybook does `setPlaybook(res.playbook)` unconditionally, and PlaybookEditor immediately calls entries.map(...) — a null state would throw at render. The save succeeded but the user sees a client crash/blank editor.
suggestion: Handle the GetPlaybook error (fall back to echoing the validated input entries, or return 200 with the trimmed entries that were actually inserted, which the service already knows without a second query).
verifyNote: Confirmed: handler.go:203 ignores GetPlaybook's error (nil slice marshals to "playbook":null since service.go:195-213 returns nil on error), page.tsx:123 sets state unconditionally, and playbook-editor.tsx:19 calls entries.map(...) on null at render with no error.tsx boundary — a hard client crash after a successful save. P2 is right: only reachable on a transient DB failure between two back-to-back queries. Fix: prefer handling the error or having SavePlaybook return the persisted entries; do NOT echo raw input, since the service drops invalid tags/empty instructions (service.go:230-233) and the echo would diverge from persisted state.

title: Manual add of compliance/routing tags has no side effects — tag state and suppression state can diverge
description: AddTag accepts any IntentVocabulary tag, including 'unsubscribe' (which domain.IsComplianceTag treats as legally-binding) and 'out_of_office'/'wrong_contact'. Intent routing (suppress/snooze/notify) only runs in the inbound-classification path, so manually tagging a conversation 'unsubscribe' inserts the row and nothing else: the conversation shows as unsubscribe in facets and the thread view, while the cadence keeps emailing the contact. This is a knock-on of the accepted 'endpoints exist, no UI yet' trade-off: the moment the tag UI ships, a user tagging unsubscribe will reasonably believe they suppressed the contact. Ownership guarding itself is correct — I verified every mutation in scope is guarded (ownConversation for tag endpoints, campaignRepo.Get for playbook, RefineDraft checks conv ownership plus draft.ConversationID and pending status before the unscoped UpdateMessageBody, and brand lessons SQL is user_id-scoped).
suggestion: Either trigger the same routing side effects for manual compliance tags (suppress on 'unsubscribe' via the existing MarkUnsubscribed path) or reject manual addition of routing-subset tags with a clear error, before the tag UI ships.

'unsubscribe' (domain/intent.go:38-51) and AddManualTag is a side-effect-free upsert (conversation/repository.go:248-257), while suppression is enforced only via contacts.unsubscribed_at (compliance.IsSuppressed at sequence/engine.go:416, campaign/scheduler.go:61) and tag routing only fires in the engine's reply branch gated on LastDirection==inbound on a still-active run (engine.go:115,166-169) — which the poller wakes and completes StoppedOnReply before a human could tag (poller.go:212-215, engine.go:135), so a manual 'unsubscribe' tag never suppresses and sends continue. P2 is correct since no UI calls addConversationTag yet (frontend/src/lib/api/outreach.ts:329 has zero component consumers); fix as suggested, noting the conversation handler/service lacks a contact.Repository dependency today, so MarkUnsubscribed must be wired in (or routing-subset tags rejected at handler.go:70) before the tag UI ships.

title: SendMessage silently discards user edits when a draft is pre-filled — UI explicitly promises 'your edits will be sent'
description: SendMessage prefers the stored draft over the request body: when req.DraftMessageID != nil it loads subject/body from the messages row and never looks at req.Subject/req.Body. The frontend handleSend always sends BOTH draft_message_id and the textarea's subject/body (conversation-thread.tsx:107-112), and the UI explicitly states 'Editing an AI draft — your edits will be sent.' (line 298-300). Result: any manual edit the user makes to an AI draft in the compose textarea (including removing '[you can edit this]' placeholder markers the prompt explicitly allows the AI to emit, fixing names, or correcting facts) is thrown away and the original unedited AI draft is emailed to a real buyer. The subject field is equally ignored, so a draft created with an empty subject (draftReplyOrFollowup sets subject "" when conv.Subject is nil, line 533-536) fails the backend's 'subject and body are required' check (line 179-180) no matter what the user types — an unrecoverable send error.
suggestion: In SendMessage, when DraftMessageID is set AND req.Body/req.Subject are non-empty, use the request values (persist them onto the draft row before sending so audit trail matches what was sent). Alternatively have the frontend stop sending draft_message_id once the user edits, but the backend fix is safer because every existing client already sends both.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:152-178 sources subject/body only from the stored draft when draft_message_id is set (req values ignored; post-send UPDATE at 246-252 never writes body/subject), while conversation-thread.tsx:107-112 always sends both and line 299 promises "your edits will be sent" — so edited AI drafts (including prompt-sanctioned "[you can edit this]" markers, outreach_reply.go:14) are emailed unedited to real recipients; the empty-subject dead-end (service.go:533-545 + 179-180) also reproduces. Backend fix as suggested is right: prefer non-empty req.Subject/req.Body on the draft path and persist them onto the draft row so the audit trail matches the sent email.

title: RefineDraft hardcodes Mode:"reply" — refining a cold opener or followup draft uses the wrong prompt, wrong guard cap, and mangles compliant drafts
description: Pending drafts have three origins: initial cold (draftInitialMessage/draftInitial, guard cap 140, guarded BEFORE WithSignature appends, service.go:395-399/743-748), sequence followup (engine.go:471-485, cap 90, never gets guidance), and reply (cap 110). RefineDraft treats them all as Mode:"reply". Traced consequences: (1) Cold draft: ConversationText is empty (the loop at 587-607 skips pending/draft rows and nothing else exists), yet the prompt instruction is 'Draft a reply to the most recent inbound message' against an empty 'Full conversation' block — the model can write as if the buyer replied ('Thanks for getting back to me'). (2) Word-cap mangling is guaranteed for longer cold drafts: a guard-clean 130-word cold body had its signature appended AFTER validation, so the stored body_text easily exceeds the reply cap of 110; refine validates the new output (which reproduces the signature from PreviousDraft) against 110 including signature words, fires length_cap, and the StricterRetry pass shortens a draft the user only asked a small tweak on. (3) Followup drafts get reply rules (40-90 words vs 30-70, exclamation allowed, 'address their question first') and a 110 cap instead of 90. (4) Guidance is loaded state-blind (line 611-613) while draftReplyOrFollowup only loads it for state=="reply" (line 514) and the sequence followup path never does — refine injects reply lessons into non-reply drafts. (5) Refine output is not passed through WithSignature, so if the model drops the signature it is silently lost from the draft.
suggestion: Re-derive state in RefineDraft exactly as DraftReply does (or read it from the draft's ai_prompt_version: outreach_draft_v1 / outreach_followup_v1 / outreach_reply_v1). Route initial drafts through BuildOutreachDraftPrompt with a revision block; pass the derived mode into replyOutreachWithGuard for followups; only load guidance for reply mode; strip/re-append the signature around the guard so the cap counts the body only.
verifyNote: Confirmed: RefineDraft hardcodes Mode:"reply" (service.go:615) yet accepts any pending draft (service.go:566-568), and the frontend Adjust UI binds to any pending_approval draft (conversation-thread.tsx:78-80) — so cold drafts (guarded at cap 140 pre-signature, service.go:395-399/743-747) and engine followups (Mode "followup", cap 90, engine.go:448) get refined with the reply prompt, reply cap 110 counting the appended signature (outreach_guard.go:71-94), empty ConversationText for cold threads (skip loop service.go:588-591 vs instruction outreach_reply.go:136), state-blind guidance (611-613 vs 514), and no WithSignature on output (631). Fix: re-derive state from sent message history as DraftReply does (service.go:346-362) — do NOT key off ai_prompt_version, since draftReplyOrFollowup stamps outreach_reply_v1 even for followups (service.go:540); strip/re-append signature around the guard.

title: Remembering a lesson while refining a cold/followup draft stores an untagged neutral lesson that contaminates ALL future neutral reply drafts for the brand
description: RememberLesson snapshots convTags + sentimentBucket of the conversation. A conversation with no inbound reply (cold opener or followup being refined) has zero conversation_tags and last_inbound_sentiment NULL, so the lesson is saved with match_tags={} and match_sentiment='neutral'. Load's matcher treats empty match_tags as a wildcard ('cardinality(match_tags)=0 OR match_tags && $3'), so a cold-opener-specific instruction like 'mention our trade-show booth in Cologne' is injected into every future neutral-sentiment reply draft for the brand, on every campaign, forever (until manually deleted via the lessons endpoint). This is a knock-on of RefineDraft being state-blind, but is independently fixable.
suggestion: In RefineDraft, only call RememberLesson when the derived draft state is 'reply' (return lesson_saved:false otherwise so the UI can grey out the checkbox), or store the draft mode on the lesson row and add 'AND mode matches' to Load's query. At minimum refuse to save a wildcard (empty-tags) lesson from a conversation that has no inbound message.
verifyNote: Confirmed: RefineDraft (service.go:557-638) has no state check and calls RememberLesson at service.go:634-636 for any pending draft, including cold/followup drafts (frontend shows the Remember checkbox for every AI draft, conversation-thread.tsx:264-280). With no inbound message, convTags is empty and sentimentBucket COALESCEs NULL to 'neutral' (loader.go:85-91), so the lesson is stored with match_tags='{}'; Load's matcher treats empty tags as a wildcard with no campaign or mode filter (loader.go:47-53; brand_reply_lessons has no mode column, migrations/000026_reply_guidance.up.sql:17-25), contaminating all future neutral reply drafts for the brand, including automated sequence replies (engine.go:313-316). Suggested fix is correct; since RefineDraft hardcodes Mode:"reply" (service.go:615), the gate must derive the real state from sent messages as DraftReply does (service.go:353-362), or persist a mode column and match it in Load.

title: RememberLesson failure is silently swallowed — user ticks 'remember', save fails, API returns success, nothing is even logged
description: `_ = replyguidance.RememberLesson(...)` discards the error entirely — not even a slog.Warn, despite RememberLesson going to the trouble of wrapping the error ('remember lesson: %w'). The handler then returns 200 with the refined message; the frontend clears the checkbox (conversation-thread.tsx:151 setRemember(false)) and the user believes the brand learned the lesson. On any transient DB error the lesson is lost with zero trace, and the user only discovers it when future drafts ignore their instruction — which they will misattribute to the AI. This directly violates the product promise of the 'Remember this for this brand' checkbox.
suggestion: At minimum log the error with conv/brand IDs. Better: return a `lesson_saved bool` in the RefineDraft response and have the frontend toast 'Draft updated, but the lesson could not be saved — try again' when false. The refine itself succeeded, so do not fail the whole request.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:635 is the sole call site of RememberLesson and discards its error (`_ =`) with no logging, even though loader.go:107 wraps it ('remember lesson: %w'); the frontend (conversation-thread.tsx:147,151) sends `remember` and clears the checkbox on any 200, so a failed save looks like success with zero trace. P1 is correct (user-visible UX/behavioral inconsistency, not a main-path correctness bug). Fix as suggested: slog.Warn with userID/brandID/convID at minimum, ideally a `lesson_saved` bool in the refine response plus a frontend toast; do not fail the whole request since the refine succeeded.

title: 30-minute AI response cache makes 'AI draft' regeneration return the byte-identical draft — DeletePendingDrafts + re-click is a no-op
description: Both draftOutreachOnce and replyOutreachOnce call CompleteJSON with a 30-minute cache TTL, and CacheKey is sha256(provider, model, system, prompt, temperature) — no user ID, no nonce, no timestamp. DraftReply deliberately wipes the pending draft and rebuilds the prompt, but if no new message has arrived the prompt is identical, so the cache returns the exact same draft. A user who clicks 'AI draft' again because they dislike the result gets the same text back and concludes the feature is broken; the non-zero temperature (0.3/0.4) that should give variety is defeated by the cache. Refine is mostly unaffected (PreviousDraft changes the prompt) but a guard-retry that fell back to the first attempt re-caches the violating output. Note the key also omits user ID entirely, so two users with identical prompts would share completions — improbable given embedded profile JSON, but a smell.
suggestion: Pass cacheTTL=0 for the generative outreach_draft/outreach_reply tasks (caching makes sense for classification/extraction, not for drafts the user may explicitly regenerate), or include the draft message UUID / an attempt counter in the prompt so regeneration busts the key.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:467/:671 pass 30m TTL and cache.go:54-58 keys on sha256(provider|model|system|prompt|temperature) only; DraftReply (service.go:328) wipes drafts but rebuilds a byte-identical prompt (no timestamps in prompt builders; context_render.go:39,60 uses day-granularity dates), so regenerate within 30 min returns the cached draft — and the cache is on by default (config.go:22 defaults REDIS_URL, main.go:114-125). Fix is correct: pass cacheTTL=0 for outreach_draft/outreach_reply at those two call sites.

title: Refine can never change the subject — instruction like 'change the subject to X' silently does nothing or leaks into the body
line: 120-124 (OutreachReplyResult has body only); repository.go:304-307 (UpdateMessageBody writes body_text only)
description: The refine pipeline is body-only end to end: the JSON output schema has no subject field, UpdateMessageBody updates only body_text, and the model is never told the draft's current subject. A user instruction targeting the subject ('make the subject line about lead times') can only be 'incorporated' by ignoring it or writing subject-like text into the body — the model has no compliant way to satisfy it. Combined with the P0 send bug, the user currently has no working path at all to change a draft's subject from the thread view (typed subject is ignored on send, refine cannot touch it). Note: the body_html staleness variant is NOT an issue — AI/campaign drafts never set body_html (only the inbound poller does) and SendMessage builds SendRequest with BodyText only (service.go:215-220).
suggestion: Either add an optional 'subject' field to the refine output schema + show the current subject in the Revision block + extend UpdateMessageBody to update it, or have the prompt explicitly state 'You can only change the body; if the instruction targets the subject, say so in needs_user_input' and surface needs_user_input in the UI (it is currently parsed and dropped).
verifyNote: Confirmed end-to-end: OutreachReplyResult is body-only (outreach_reply.go:120-124), the Revision block shows only the previous body and the transcript loop skips the pending draft so the model never sees its subject (service.go:570-573, 589; outreach_reply.go:160-163), UpdateMessageBody writes only body_text (repository.go:304-307), and NeedsUserInput is parsed then dropped (service.go:627-637, handler.go:356-361); the no-path-to-change-subject claim also holds since SendMessage ignores req.Subject when draft_message_id is set (service.go:152-172) and conversation-thread.tsx:107-109 always passes it. P2 is the honest severity (design gap, not a malfunction); the suggested fix is correct — minimally, surface needs_user_input and tell the model the body is the only editable field, or fully add an optional subject output + extend UpdateMessageBody.

title: Lessons: no dedup against playbook or each other, LIMIT 6 silently evicts older lessons, and DESC ordering puts the newest lesson in the weakest prompt position on conflicts
description: Load concatenates playbook lines and lessons into one flat bullet list. Verified behaviors: (1) remembering the same instruction on two conversations inserts duplicate rows (RememberLesson is a plain INSERT) and both are injected, also duplicating any identical playbook line; (2) contradictory lessons ('be more formal' then 'be casual') both match the same bucket and are both injected with no precedence statement — and because ORDER BY created_at DESC renders newest FIRST while LLMs weight later prompt text more, the OLD lesson sits closest to the output and tends to win, the inverse of user intent; (3) once a brand has >6 lessons in one sentiment bucket, the 7th-oldest silently stops applying (lessonLimit=6) — the user notices the brand 'forgot' a lesson with no UI signal.
suggestion: Dedupe on normalized instruction text (and against playbook lines), reverse to chronological order after LIMIT so the newest lesson renders last, and append one line to the guidance header: 'If instructions conflict, the later one wins.' Surface 'only the 6 most recent lessons apply' in the brand lessons UI.
