verifyNote: Confirmed: RememberLesson is a plain INSERT with no unique constraint (loader.go:101-105, migration 000026) and Load appends playbook+lessons with no dedup (loader.go:37,58); ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 6 (loader.go:16,51) renders newest first with no precedence statement in the prompt header (outreach_reply.go:157); and the frontend LearnedLessonsCard (sender-profile-editor.tsx:417-462) lists all lessons unlimited with no hint of the 6-per-bucket cap, so evicted lessons appear active but are ignored. P2 is the honest severity (no correctness break; recency-bias effect is heuristic), and the suggested fix — dedupe normalized text, reverse to chronological after LIMIT, add a "later instruction wins" line, surface the cap in the UI — is correct.

title: User-authored guidance/instruction text is inserted into the prompt unsanitized — multi-line lessons can forge new '## ' prompt sections, and the guard cannot catch fabricated pricing
description: Playbook instructions, lessons, and the refine instruction are interpolated verbatim: Load only does '- '+TrimSpace (embedded newlines survive, so a lesson containing '## Task mode\nfollowup' or '## Revision request' visually becomes a top-level prompt section), and BuildOutreachReplyPrompt inserts RefineInstruction raw after 'The user wants this change:'. There is no length cap anywhere — handler.RefineDraft only checks non-empty, so a 50KB instruction goes into both the prompt and brand_reply_lessons verbatim. Risk is low (own-account, own outbound email) but the no-hallucination defense for prices/terms is purely prompt-level: ValidateOutreachBody checks only catalog hedging, filler phrases, exclamations and length, so a naive lesson like 'always quote $2.50/kg FOB' (or one remembered months ago and forgotten) forces a committed price into every matching draft and the guard passes it. The guidance header's '(follow them; still never invent facts)' is the only mitigation, and a lesson IS user-provided so the model reasonably treats the number as fact.
suggestion: Sanitize on injection: collapse newlines to spaces in lesson/playbook/instruction text, cap length (~300 chars, enforced at RememberLesson and the playbook upsert), and strip leading '#'. Optionally add a guard regex for currency-amount + commitment patterns when the conversation contains no prior user-stated price, downgrading to needs_user_input instead of a hard rewrite.
verifyNote: Confirmed: loader.go:36-37/56-58 only TrimSpace (embedded newlines survive into the '## '-sectioned prompt), outreach_reply.go:156-163 appends guidance and RefineInstruction raw, handler.go:352-355 and SavePlaybook (group/service.go:230-239) have no length cap (columns are TEXT), and outreach_guard.go:32-82 checks only catalog-hedging/filler/exclamation/length — no price-commitment check. P2 is the honest rating despite the auto-send path at sequence/engine.go:462-486 (guidance-tainted followups can send unreviewed) because all text is account-owner-authored; the suggested fix is right, but apply newline-collapse at read time in Load as well so existing rows are sanitized.

title: Second browser tab never shows a refined draft body — pre-fill effect is guarded by `pending && !draftMsgID` and UpdateMessageBody leaves no change signal
description: The active tab is fine: handleAdjust sets body from the refine response (line 149). But any other open tab pre-filled the textarea once (draftMsgID set), and every subsequent SWR revalidation (60s refreshInterval, SSE-triggered mutate) hits `pending && !draftMsgID` == false, so the stale v1 body stays in the textarea forever even though data.messages now carries v2. Pending drafts are filtered out of the bubble list (line 160), so there is no other place the refreshed text could appear. UpdateMessageBody bumps nothing (messages have no updated_at column; conversations.updated_at untouched), so the client has no cheap signal either. Sending from the stale tab actually emails the refined v2 (backend reads the stored draft — the P0 flip side), i.e. the user sends text they have never seen.
suggestion: Track the last server body in a ref; on each SWR refresh, if the pending draft's body_text changed AND the textarea is not dirty (user hasn't typed since last sync), update state. Adding updated_at to messages (bumped in UpdateMessageBody) would make the comparison robust.
verifyNote: Confirmed: conversation-thread.tsx:79 guard `pending && !draftMsgID` blocks re-sync after the first pre-fill, line 160 hides pending drafts from bubbles, and UpdateMessageBody (internal/outreach/conversation/repository.go:304-307) only sets body_text on a table with no updated_at (migration 000009), so a second tab keeps stale v1 forever; service.go:152-174 confirms a send from that tab emails the stored v2 the user never saw. P2 is appropriate since it needs two simultaneous views and the unseen-send root cause is the separate draft-precedence P0; the suggested dirty-aware re-sync plus messages.updated_at fix is correct.

title: replyguidance.Load and sentimentBucket swallow all DB errors — guidance silently absent and lessons mis-bucketed with no log line
description: Both queries in Load use `if err == nil { ... }` with no else, convTags returns nil on error, and sentimentBucket ignores the QueryRow error with `_ =`. On any transient failure the draft is generated with zero guidance — the user's playbook and remembered lessons are simply not applied — and nothing is logged, making 'the AI ignored my playbook' reports undiagnosable. Same pattern as the swallowed RememberLesson but on the read path; also rows.Err() is never checked, so a mid-iteration failure truncates the lesson list silently.
suggestion: slog.Warn with conv/campaign/brand IDs on each error path (guidance should stay best-effort — don't fail the draft), and check rows.Err() after iteration. Consider returning (guidance string, degraded bool) so callers can record that a draft was generated without guidance.
verifyNote: Confirmed: loader.go:33 and :54 use `if err == nil` with no else/log, convTags (loader.go:69-71) returns nil on error, sentimentBucket (loader.go:87-89) discards the QueryRow error via `_ =` (silently defaulting to "neutral"), and rows.Err() is never checked after any of the three iteration loops; the package has zero logging and Load returns only a string, so callers (conversation/service.go:515,612; sequence/engine.go:315) generate drafts with empty guidance on any transient DB failure with no trace. P2 is the right severity (best-effort path, observability smell); the suggested slog.Warn-with-IDs plus rows.Err() check is the correct fix.

title: Engine validates reply-mode drafts with the followup guard (90-word cap); conversation service uses the reply guard (110) — engine is wrong, sim copies the engine
description: Engine.draftReplyForApproval builds OutreachReplyInput with Mode:"reply" (engine.go:317) but followupWithGuard hardcodes prompts.DraftModeFollowup (engine.go:547). So every production auto-drafted reply on the campaign reply branch is validated against the 90-word followup cap instead of the 110-word reply cap, and the followup-only tolerance for "circle back"/"touch base" (outreach_guard.go:53) wrongly applies to replies. The conversation service's replyOutreachWithGuard (conversation/service.go:649-652) picks the mode from in.Mode, so when the user refines that same draft via POST /draft/refine the 110-cap reply rules apply and "circle back" becomes forbidden — the identical draft is judged by two different rulebooks depending on which component touches it (spurious StricterRetry calls, extra AI cost, terser engine drafts). The sim's draftFollowup (aicalls.go:60) also hardcodes DraftModeFollowup for its Mode:"reply" calls, so the Lab faithfully mirrors the engine's bug but diverges from the refine path users actually exercise. The engine is the wrong party.
suggestion: In Engine.followupWithGuard derive the guard mode from in.Mode exactly like conversation.Service.replyOutreachWithGuard (mode := DraftModeReply; if in.Mode == "followup" { mode = DraftModeFollowup }). Apply the same fix to simulation/aicalls.go draftFollowup so the Lab tracks the corrected behavior.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:547 hardcodes DraftModeFollowup while draftReplyForApproval passes Mode:"reply" (engine.go:317-318), whereas conversation/service.go:649-652 correctly derives the mode from in.Mode — so the same draft is guarded at 90 words with "circle back" tolerated when engine-drafted, but at 110 words with "circle back" forbidden when refined via RefineDraft (service.go:615); simulation/service.go:265-266 + aicalls.go:60 mirror the engine bug. P1 (not P0): drafts still reach pending_approval for human review, so impact is spurious retries/AI cost and inconsistent rulebooks. The suggested fix is correct — copy the mode-derivation pattern from replyOutreachWithGuard into Engine.followupWithGuard and simulation draftFollowup.

title: Sim OOO path wipes ALL intent tags; production deletes only the out_of_office tag and re-routes on the surviving tags after the snooze
description: On RouteSnooze the sim sets `tags = nil` and falls through to the sentiment branch within the same handleReply call. Production deletes ONLY conversation_tags row tag='out_of_office' (engine.go:179-182), snoozes via BumpRun, and 3 days later re-enters handleReplyBranch which re-reads ALL remaining tags from the DB (loadConvTags, engine.go:166). Two divergences: (1) routing — if the classifier emitted e.g. wrong_contact or unsubscribe-adjacent tags alongside out_of_office, prod routes on them after the snooze (RouteNotify/RouteSuppress), while the sim always lands on the sentiment branch; (2) guidance — the sim's simGuidance call (service.go:274) receives tags=nil so all playbook lines and tag-matched lessons are dropped from the resume draft, whereas prod's replyguidance.Load reads the persisted tags (loader.go:22, 28-42) and injects matching playbook/lessons. The Lab's OOO-resume drafts are systematically less guided than prod's.
suggestion: Replace `tags = nil` with removing only domain.TagOutOfOffice from the slice (mirror the targeted DELETE), then re-run ResolveIntentRouting on the remaining tags before falling through to the sentiment branch, and pass the surviving tags to simGuidance.
verifyNote: Confirmed: sim sets tags=nil and falls through to the sentiment branch in the same handleReply call (service.go:240-247), passing nil tags to simGuidance (service.go:274,391-397) which drops all playbook lines and tag-matched lessons; prod deletes only the out_of_office row (engine.go:179-182), BumpRuns, and on resume re-reads all surviving tags (engine.go:117-125,166,216-229) so a co-emitted wrong_contact routes to RouteNotify and replyguidance.Load (engine.go:315, loader.go:22-53) injects tag-matched guidance — the classifier does emit multi-tag results (aicalls.go:90-97). Two caveats: the "unsubscribe-adjacent" example is impossible (unsubscribe wins precedence pre-snooze in both, trigger.go:75-84) and the guidance gap only manifests for OOO replies carrying additional tags (OOO-only replies behave identically). Fix as suggested — remove only domain.TagOutOfOffice, re-run ResolveIntentRouting (only RouteNotify/RouteSentiment are then reachable), and pass surviving tags to simGuidance.

title: Sim treats every cadence followup as instantly sent; production queues it pending_approval unless step.AutoSend && a prior sent outbound exists
description: The sim's SequenceActionSendMessage case drafts a followup, appends it to the transcript as a delivered 'you' message, advances lastAt, and lets the persona reply to it. Production's actionSendMessage only sends when `canAutoSend := step.AutoSend && hasHumanSent(msgs)` (engine.go:464); otherwise the draft is created with Status=pending_approval and is NOT sent — the recipient never sees it until a human approves, and conversations.last_message_at is not bumped (UpdateLast only runs on the auto-send path, engine.go:533). The sim never reads step.AutoSend at all (RunInput.Steps carries it; the Lab UI defaults auto_send:false on every step, frontend simulation/page.tsx:65-69). So every default Lab run models a cadence prod would pause at the first followup awaiting approval — day labels, slow_warmer touch timing, and 'no_reply → cold' outcomes all assume instant approval that prod doesn't give.
suggestion: Honor step.AutoSend in the sim loop: when false, either model it as sent-after-approval and add an event line ('queued for approval — assuming approved same day'), or stop the cadence as prod effectively does. At minimum surface the assumption in the transcript so users don't read the Lab as literal prod timing.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:464/471-486 queues followups as pending_approval (no send, UpdateLast only at :533) unless step.AutoSend && hasHumanSent, while the sim (service.go:297-314) sends every followup instantly and the simulation package has zero AutoSend references despite RunInput.Steps carrying it (domain/outreach.go:300); the Lab UI defaults auto_send:false on all steps (frontend/src/app/(dashboard)/simulation/page.tsx:66-68). P1 is correct — sim is advisory so not P0, but it misrepresents prod timing/outcomes, and the sim explicitly aims for prod parity elsewhere (service.go:235-238). Fix as suggested; minimal version is an event transcript line ("queued for approval — assuming approved same day") when !step.AutoSend, matching the existing event-line pattern.

title: Sim applies ALL matching brand lessons; production caps lessons at the 6 most recent
description: simGuidance loops over every lesson from sender.ListLessons (which has no LIMIT — sender/repository.go:54-58) and appends every one matching sentiment bucket + tag overlap. Production's replyguidance.Load runs the same match in SQL but with ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 6 (lessonLimit, loader.go:16). For a brand with more than 6 matching lessons, Lab drafts are steered by guidance lines prod would silently drop, so the Lab overstates how much accumulated lessons shape real drafts — exactly the thing the lessons feature is in the Lab to test. (Tag/sentiment matching semantics are otherwise equivalent: cardinality(match_tags)=0 OR overlap, same bucket source — poller writes LegacyForScore(score) to last_inbound_sentiment, which equals the sim's in-memory `sent`.)
suggestion: In simGuidance, stop after 6 matched lessons (ListLessons already returns created_at DESC, so taking the first 6 matches reproduces prod exactly), or extract a shared pure matching helper used by both loader.go and the sim.
verifyNote: Confirmed: simGuidance (simulation/service.go:398-407) appends every matching lesson from ListLessons (sender/repository.go:54-58, no LIMIT, created_at DESC), while prod's replyguidance.Load caps at 6 via ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $4 with lessonLimit=6 (loader.go:16, 47-52); match semantics and sentiment-bucket source are otherwise identical (poller.go:271 writes LegacyForScore to last_inbound_sentiment, equal to the sim's sent from aicalls.go:89). Fix as suggested: break after 6 matches in the sim loop — since both sources are created_at DESC and prod filters before limiting, taking the first 6 matches reproduces prod exactly.

title: Sim forces the unsubscribe tag deterministically and does not model the poller's keyword opt-out net — overstating unsubscribe routing reliability
description: handleReply appends domain.TagUnsubscribe whenever persona.unsubscribes or the persona-bot's self-reported intent is "unsubscribing" — regardless of what the real classifier emitted. In production RouteSuppress fires only if the classifier emits tag_unsubscribe with confidence >= 0.5; if it misses, the safety net is the poller's LooksLikeOptOut keyword scan, which marks the CONTACT unsubscribed (poller.go:226-230) but writes no conversation tag — so the engine's reply branch still takes the sentiment path (likely negative → mark cold), a materially different prod flow (no 'suppressed' routing, possible auto-draft on a neutral-scored opt-out). The Lab therefore (a) reports 100% unsubscribe routing for the unsubscriber persona even when the classifier would miss in prod, and (b) can never surface the real prod inconsistency where the keyword net suppresses the contact while the conversation routes by sentiment. The Lab's headline claim (classifier fidelity, 'same vocabulary + confidence floor as the poller' per aicalls.go:69-73) is undermined for exactly the compliance-critical tag.
suggestion: Drop the forced-tag override (or make it opt-in 'deterministic mode') and instead mirror prod's two nets: run compliance.LooksLikeOptOut on the persona reply body and, when it hits without the classifier tag, emit an event line showing the keyword-net path (contact suppressed, sentiment branch still taken). Track classifier tag-miss rate in the summary like SentimentAccuracy.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:217-220 unconditionally appends domain.TagUnsubscribe for the unsubscriber persona (personas.go:56) so RouteSuppress always fires in the sim, masking classifier misses; in prod the engine routes only on conversation_tags (engine.go:166, 216-230) and the poller's keyword net (poller.go:226-230) suppresses the contact without writing a tag, so a miss takes the sentiment branch and can queue a pending-approval draft for an opted-out contact (engine.go:211, 287-296, no IsSuppressed check) — exactly as described, contradicting aicalls.go:69-73's "exact production path" claim; LooksLikeOptOut is unreferenced in the simulation package. P1 (not P0) because the sim never sends and prod still suppresses the contact via the keyword net; the fix (drop/gate the override, mirror LooksLikeOptOut with an event line, add tag-miss rate to Summary) is sound.

title: Data race: len(results) read outside the mutex in the errgroup progress event
description: Run's worker goroutines (g.SetLimit(4)) append to `results` under `mu`, but the broker.Publish call at line 141 reads `len(results)` after mu.Unlock() — a concurrent read of the slice header while other goroutines append under the lock. This is a genuine Go data race (would be flagged by -race); practical impact is a wrong/torn 'done' count in the SSE progress event.
suggestion: Capture `done := len(results)` inside the mu.Lock/Unlock critical section and pass the captured value to broker.Publish.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:132-142 — `len(results)` at line 141 is read after mu.Unlock() (line 138) while up to 4 sibling goroutines append to `results` under mu (line 133), an unsynchronized read/write on the slice header that -race would flag; impact is limited to the `done` count in the SSE progress event (final aggregate at line 152 runs after g.Wait() and is safe). Fix as suggested: capture `done := len(results)` inside the critical section and pass it to broker.Publish, keeping Publish outside the lock.

title: Sim cold draft ignores the campaign AttachCatalog gate, positioning, and prior-conversation context that production cold drafts use
description: The sim sets HasCatalog purely from leadctx.SenderHasCatalog(brand) (service.go:174), but production cold drafts gate on campaign.AttachCatalog first and only then confirm the file exists (drafter.go:87-94). RunInput has no AttachCatalog knob, so for any brand with an uploaded catalog the Lab always drafts catalog-attached cold emails (different prompt, catalog-hedge guard active) even when the user's real campaigns have AttachCatalog=false. The prod drafter also injects CampaignPositioning (campaign goal / positioning overrides, drafter.go:100-105, 116-126) and PriorConversationsContext (warm re-engage path, drafter.go:110-114) — neither is representable in the Lab, so the tested touch-0 draft is a systematically different prompt than the prod campaign drafter's. (Follow-up/reply paths are unaffected: engine and conversation service also use SenderHasCatalog-style checks.)
suggestion: Add attach_catalog (and optionally a positioning/goal string) to RunInput, defaulting attach_catalog to false to match a fresh campaign; compute hasCatalog = attachCatalog && SenderHasCatalog(brand) exactly like drafter.go.
verifyNote: Confirmed: simulation/service.go:174 derives HasCatalog solely from leadctx.SenderHasCatalog(brand) and RunInput (service.go:41-53) has no attach_catalog/positioning knob, while the prod cold drafter gates on camp.AttachCatalog before checking the file (campaign/drafter.go:87-94) and injects CampaignPositioning and PriorConversationsContext (drafter.go:100-126) that the sim's draftIn (service.go:193-201) never sets; these fields demonstrably change the prompt (prompts/outreach_draft.go:158-176) and the guard input. The suggested fix is correct, with one refinement: apply attach_catalog && SenderHasCatalog only to the touch-0 cold draft, keeping the followup/reply hasCatalog unchanged since engine.go:311,445 use SenderHasCatalog without a campaign gate.

title: Lab presents 'cold' and 'unsubscribed' as distinct outcomes, but production's cadence mark_cold action actually suppresses the contact (MarkUnsubscribed)
description: Production has two different 'cold' semantics: the reply-branch negative default sets campaign_contacts.status='cold' (campaign-scoped, engine.go:201-203), while the cadence SequenceActionMarkCold calls contacts.MarkUnsubscribed(ctx, contactID, "sequence_marked_cold") (engine.go:371-372) — a contact-level compliance suppression identical in effect to an unsubscribe (compliance.IsSuppressed blocks all future sends). The sim maps BOTH to outcome "cold" (deriveOutcome) and reserves "unsubscribed" for the suppress route, so the Lab teaches users that an exhausted cadence leaves a recoverable 'cold' lead when prod has actually suppressed the contact globally. This is a knock-on inconsistency of prod's mark_cold→MarkUnsubscribed mapping that the Lab masks rather than mirrors. (Also: prod advances to the next step after mark_cold rather than breaking immediately, but the IsSuppressed check makes that behaviorally equivalent.)
suggestion: Either align prod (mark_cold should set campaign_contacts status, not MarkUnsubscribed) or make the Lab honest: when the cadence mark_cold fires, emit an event line noting the contact is suppressed from ALL future outreach in production, and/or use a distinct outcome key (with a matching OUTCOME_COLORS entry).
verifyNote: Confirmed: prod's cadence mark_cold calls contacts.MarkUnsubscribed (sequence/engine.go:371-372), permanently setting contacts.unsubscribed_at (contact/repository.go:429-438) which compliance.IsSuppressed (unsubscribe.go:101-103) uses to block all future sends (campaign/scheduler.go:61, engine.go:416), while the reply-branch mark_cold only sets campaign-scoped campaign_contacts.status='cold' (engine.go:201-203); the sim maps both to outcome "cold" (simulation/service.go:315-317, 252-253, 334-349) and the UI renders "cold" benignly vs red "unsubscribed" (simulation/page.tsx:45-46), so the Lab does mask the global suppression. Kept at P2: it's a parity/teaching gap in a sandbox feature with no production impact; the minimal fix is the suggested transcript event line at service.go:317 noting the contact is suppressed from all future outreach (and separately question prod's reuse of the unsubscribe flag for cadence exhaustion).

title: Sim classifier skips the poller's score clamp and empty-body short-circuit
description: Poller.classifyReply clamps the model score to [-1,1] (clampScore, poller.go:265) and returns neutral without an AI call when the body is whitespace-only (poller.go:253). The sim's classify uses out.Score unclamped and always calls the model. Because LabelForScore/LegacyForScore thresholds saturate, an out-of-range score yields the same label/legacy bucket in both, so branch routing cannot diverge — but the raw score (used for the 5-level display and stored in transcripts) can exceed [-1,1] only in the Lab, and an empty persona body classifies via AI in the Lab vs hard-neutral in prod. Minor, but the file's own comment claims 'the exact production path' (aicalls.go:72-73).
suggestion: Apply the same clamp (extract clampScore into a shared package or domain) and short-circuit empty bodies to neutral in simulation classify, matching poller.classifyReply line-for-line.
verifyNote: Confirmed: sim classify (aicalls.go:84) skips the clamp (poller.go:265, 287-296) and the empty-body neutral short-circuit (poller.go:253), despite aicalls.go:72-73 claiming "the exact production path"; LabelForScore/LegacyForScore saturation (sentiment.go:28-41, 60-68) means routing can't diverge, as the finding says. One overstatement: the unclamped score is never displayed or stored in the Lab — service.go:216 discards it and TranscriptMessage (repository.go:18-26) has no score field — so the only observable gap is the empty-body AI call. Fix as suggested: move clampScore into domain beside LabelForScore and add a TrimSpace(body)=="" neutral return in sim classify.

title: Legacy-sentiment rows: badge renders but sentiment facet predicate and counts ignore them
description: The row badge falls back to the legacy 3-value string (SentimentBadge: `const level = label ?? levelFromLegacy(legacy)`), so a pre-migration reply with last_inbound_sentiment='positive' and last_inbound_sentiment_label=NULL shows a 'Positive' badge. But buildFacetWhere filters only `cv.last_inbound_sentiment_label = ANY($n)` and facetCounts counts only `FILTER (WHERE cv.last_inbound_sentiment_label = '...')`. Result: clicking the Positive chip excludes rows that visibly carry a Positive badge, and the chip count is lower than the number of badges on screen. Users triaging by sentiment will silently miss real positive replies. This is the knock-on inconsistency of the accepted no-backfill trade-off, not the trade-off itself.
suggestion: Define one shared SQL expression in service.go, e.g. `effLabel := "COALESCE(cv.last_inbound_sentiment_label, CASE cv.last_inbound_sentiment WHEN 'positive' THEN 'positive' WHEN 'neutral' THEN 'neutral' WHEN 'negative' THEN 'negative' END)"`, and use it in both buildFacetWhere (`effLabel = ANY($n)`) and every facetCounts FILTER clause. This mirrors levelFromLegacy exactly (legacy 'negative' -> level 'negative'), so badge, filter, and counts agree without backfilling data.
verifyNote: Confirmed: migration 000025 adds last_inbound_sentiment_label with no backfill, the group page (groups/[groupId]/page.tsx:366-370) plus sentiment-badge.tsx:19 render badges from the legacy 3-value column, while buildFacetWhere (service.go:395) and facetCounts (service.go:446-450) match only the label column — so legacy rows show badges but are excluded from sentiment filters/counts. Downgraded to P1: affects only the bounded, self-healing pre-migration-25 row set (repository.go:282 writes all three columns on every new reply) and rows stay visible when unfiltered. The suggested shared COALESCE(label, CASE legacy ...) expression in both buildFacetWhere and the FILTER clauses is correct and mirrors levelFromLegacy exactly; a one-time backfill UPDATE would be an equally valid simpler fix if the no-backfill decision is revisited.

title: Unsaved cadence-step edits are clobbered by the 10s group poll / any action refresh
description: `useEffect(() => { if (group?.steps) setSteps(group.steps); }, [group?.steps])` re-syncs local edit state whenever the SWR data object is replaced. The group SWR has refreshInterval:10000, and SWR's deep-compare only preserves the old object when the whole payload is unchanged — but GroupDetail includes sent_count/replied_count/facet_counts/notifications/last_message_at, which change continuously while a group is active. Any such change yields a new `group.steps` array reference, the effect fires, and setSteps wipes the user's in-progress cadence edits. The same happens immediately after any button via action()->refresh()->mutateGroup (e.g. approving one email mid-edit). The playbook effect (114-116) has the same shape but its SWR key has no refreshInterval, so it only bites on focus-revalidate when server data actually changed.
suggestion: Track a dirty flag for the steps editor and skip the sync effect while dirty (or only initialize once per groupId, e.g. seed state in a keyed child component or compare serialized steps before overwriting). Re-sync from the server only after a successful saveSteps. Apply the same guard to the playbook effect for symmetry.
verifyNote: Confirmed: page.tsx:101-103 re-runs setSteps(group.steps) whenever the 10s-polled group SWR (page.tsx:71-75) returns any changed payload — GroupDetail carries continuously-changing counts/facet_counts/notifications (outreach.ts:165-173, 316-320), and FollowupStepEditor is fully controlled (followup-step-editor.tsx:13-19), so unsaved cadence edits are visibly wiped; action()->refresh()->mutateGroup (page.tsx:143-158) triggers the same wipe after any button. Downgraded P0->P1: only unsaved local form state is lost (recoverable, no persisted-data corruption); the suggested dirty-flag/seed-once-per-groupId fix plus re-sync from the patchGroupSteps response in saveSteps is correct (apply same to playbook effect at 114-116).

title: Sentiment badge hidden once you reply (last_direction='out'), yet the sentiment facet still matches the row
description: The badge renders only when `e.last_direction === "in"`. After the buyer replies and the user sends the approved auto-draft, last_direction flips to 'out' while last_inbound_sentiment_label stays set. The backend sentiment predicate and counts have no direction condition, so filtering by 'Positive' returns these rows — displayed with no sentiment badge at all. The inverse of the legacy mismatch: filtered list shows rows that appear to have no sentiment, and chip counts exceed visible badges. Intent tag chips on the same rows are NOT direction-gated, making the badge's disappearance look like a glitch.
suggestion: Drop the `last_direction === "in"` gate and render SentimentBadge whenever sentiment_label/sentiment is non-null — the field's semantics are already 'last inbound sentiment', so it is meaningful after you reply. If you want to flag 'awaiting your reply', do that with the existing unread/status indicators instead.
verifyNote: Confirmed: page.tsx:365 gates SentimentBadge on last_direction==="in" while the backend sentiment predicate (group/service.go:395) and facet counts (446-450) ignore direction, and last_inbound_sentiment* is only ever written by SetInboundClassification (conversation/repository.go:280-287) and never cleared when outbound sends flip last_direction to 'out' (conversation/service.go:288, sequence/engine.go:533) — so sentiment-filtered rows can show no badge. The suggested fix is correct and safe: SentimentBadge already returns null on missing sentiment (sentiment-badge.tsx:20), and the inbox list (conversation-list-item.tsx:69) already renders it ungated, so dropping the gate also restores cross-page consistency.

title: Structurally-empty facet combo (sentiment + 'No reply') is selectable with no hint
description: no_reply maps to `cc.status = 'sent' AND cv.last_direction = 'out'`, i.e. no inbound message exists, so last_inbound_sentiment_label is necessarily NULL. AND-across-facets means any sentiment chip + the 'No reply' chip always returns zero rows. The bar happily renders both as active and the list shows the generic 'No emails in this filter.' — the user can't tell whether their pipeline is empty or the combo is impossible. Same trap for intent tags + 'No reply' (tags only exist after an inbound is classified).
suggestion: When 'No reply' is the sole status selection, disable (or visually mute with a tooltip 'No-reply rows have no sentiment/tags yet') the sentiment and intent chips, and vice versa; alternatively replace the empty-state copy with '"No reply" can't be combined with sentiment/intent filters — contacts who haven't replied have no classified reply.'
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:426-427 maps no_reply to (cc.status='sent' AND cv.last_direction='out'), and the only writer of last_inbound_sentiment_label (conversation/repository.go:280-287, called from poller.go:196-209) simultaneously sets last_direction='in' and cc.status='replied', so sentiment + 'No reply' is structurally zero-row; facet-filter-bar.tsx:69-98 renders all chips with counts and no disable/hint, and page.tsx:330-333 shows only the generic 'No emails in this filter.' empty state. One correction: intent tags are NOT strictly inbound-only (manual tags via POST /conversations/{id}/tags, handler.go:38), so prefer the suggested contextual empty-state copy fix — and hard-disable only the sentiment chips, muting (not disabling) tag chips.

title: tags.slice(0,3) silently truncates intent chips with no '+N' overflow — alphabetical order hides routing tags
line: 372 (also simulation/page.tsx:492-494; ordering: backend service.go:357 ORDER BY tag)
description: Both the group page row and the sim LeadRow render `tags.slice(0, 3)` with no indicator that more exist. The backend returns tags alphabetically (`ORDER BY tag`), so on a row with 4+ tags, late-alphabet high-stakes tags — 'unsubscribe', 'wrong_contact', 'timing_objection', 'shipping_question' — are exactly the ones dropped (e.g. ['info_requested','meeting_requested','price_requested','unsubscribe'] hides 'unsubscribe'). A user can act on a contact without seeing a compliance-critical signal, and the tag facet will match rows whose chip isn't visible.
suggestion: Append a `+{tags.length - 3}` chip with a title/tooltip listing the remaining tags (a trivial Badge), and/or sort routing-class tags first client-side via the INTENT_TAGS class metadata before slicing so unsubscribe/wrong_contact always surface.
verifyNote: Confirmed: tags.slice(0,3) with no overflow at groups/[groupId]/page.tsx:372, simulation/page.tsx:492-494, and a third uncited site conversation-list-item.tsx:71; backend sorts alphabetically (group/service.go:357, conversation/repository.go:166) and tags accumulate uncapped from a 16-tag vocabulary (conversation/repository.go:289-297), while the tag facet matches all tags at SQL level (service.go:400) so filtered rows can hide the matching chip — a real user-visible inconsistency. One overstatement: unsubscribe is auto-suppressed server-side on the AI tag (sequence/engine.go:168-169) and via keywords (poller/poller.go:226-228), so it's not a compliance breach, just hidden context. The suggested fix is sound and feasible — INTENT_TAGS class metadata already exists at frontend/src/components/outreach/intent-tags.ts:13-33; apply the +N chip and routing-first sort at all three render sites.

title: Mixed save models on group page: playbook and cadence edits lost on navigation with no dirty warning
description: Inventory: cadence steps -> explicit 'Save cadence' button (449); playbook -> explicit 'Save playbook' button (491); positive/negative branch selects -> auto-save onChange via saveBranches (465, 476); attach-catalog checkbox -> auto-save via action() (305). Two adjacent controls in the same 'When they reply' card behave differently: the branch selects persist instantly while the playbook below them does not. Neither buffered editor tracks dirty state, and there is no beforeunload handler or router guard anywhere on the page — clicking any sidebar link or the group list discards playbook/cadence edits silently. Combined with the poll-clobber bug (separate finding), buffered edits on this page are fragile in two independent ways.
suggestion: Track dirty state for steps and playbook (compare against last-fetched values); show it on the buttons ('Save cadence •' / disable when clean), and register a beforeunload + Next.js navigation guard while dirty. Longer term, unify the card to one model — either debounce-auto-save the playbook/steps like the selects, or make the selects part of an explicit save.
verifyNote: Confirmed: page.tsx buffers steps/playbook with explicit save buttons (449, 491) while adjacent branch selects auto-save onChange (465/476 -> updateGroupBranches at 136) and the catalog checkbox auto-saves (305); grep across frontend/src finds zero beforeunload/dirty/navigation-guard code, so navigating away silently discards typed playbook text and cadence edits. P1 stands; the suggested dirty-tracking + unload-guard fix is correct, but note the app uses the Next App Router (no router.events), so the soft-nav guard needs link interception or an equivalent hook alongside beforeunload.

title: Sim OUTCOME_COLORS (and persona toggles) have no dark-mode variants and use off-theme palette
description: The app supports dark mode (globals.css:5 `@custom-variant dark`, .dark block at :88; indigo oklch primary). CLASS_STYLE (intent-tags.ts:42-46) and all five SENTIMENT_META entries (intent-tags.ts:63-92) ship dark: variants — verified complete. But OUTCOME_COLORS uses light-only classes ('border-green-300 text-green-700 bg-green-50' etc. for all 7 outcomes): in dark mode the outcome badges render bright pastel pills clashing with the dark card, inconsistent with the sentiment/tag chips beside them on the same row. The persona toggle buttons (border-blue-400 bg-blue-50 text-blue-700) have the same problem and also use raw blue instead of the primary token, unlike FacetChip which correctly uses border-primary/bg-primary/10/text-primary. Also replied_positive uses 'green' while the sentiment system uses 'emerald' — two different greens side by side.
suggestion: Move OUTCOME_COLORS next to CLASS_STYLE/SENTIMENT_META in intent-tags.ts and follow the same pattern, e.g. 'border-emerald-300/60 text-emerald-700 bg-emerald-50 dark:bg-emerald-500/10 dark:text-emerald-300'; switch the persona toggle active state to the FacetChip primary-token classes (or reuse FacetChip outright).
verifyNote: Confirmed: OUTCOME_COLORS (simulation/page.tsx:40-48) and the persona-toggle active state (page.tsx:226) are light-only and use raw green/blue, while dark mode is real and user-toggleable (globals.css:5,88; theme-provider.tsx:21; settings/page.tsx:18) and the adjacent SentimentBadge/TagChip on the same LeadRow (page.tsx:491-495) are fully dark-aware via intent-tags.ts:42-46,63-92; FacetChip (facet-filter-bar.tsx:33-34) uses primary tokens, and the green-vs-emerald mismatch is also accurate. Suggested fix is correct; prefer reusing the already-exported FacetChip for the persona toggles and adding dark: variants (emerald pattern) to OUTCOME_COLORS in intent-tags.ts.

title: Sim ResultView lastReply() skips the legacy-sentiment fallback the transcript badge uses
description: lastReply returns `t[i].sentiment_level ?? null` with no levelFromLegacy fallback, while the transcript bubble renders `<SentimentBadge label={m.sentiment_level} legacy={m.sentiment} />` (530) — SimMessage's `sentiment` legacy field exists in the type (simulation.ts:13). For any sim message carrying only the legacy value, the expanded transcript shows a sentiment badge but the LeadRow shows none, the sentiment facet count skips it, and the sentiment filter excludes it. This reproduces inside the Lab the exact badge-vs-facet divergence of the live group page, undermining the 'sim mirrors production' promise.
suggestion: In lastReply, return `{ level: t[i].sentiment_level ?? levelFromLegacy(t[i].sentiment), tags: ... }` (levelFromLegacy is already exported from intent-tags.ts), and pass the same resolved level to LeadRow so row badge, counts, and filter use one resolution path — matching whatever fix lands for the backend facet predicate.
verifyNote: The asymmetry exists as cited (page.tsx:328 lacks the levelFromLegacy fallback that line 530 gets via sentiment-badge.tsx:19), but it is unreachable: the only backend writer of "them" sim messages (backend-go/internal/outreach/simulation/service.go:221) always sets both Sentiment and SentimentLevel, classify/LabelForScore (aicalls.go:74-99, domain/sentiment.go:28-41) can never yield an empty level, the feature is entirely uncommitted (no legacy data era), and the local simulation_leads table is empty (0 rows, 0 legacy-only). Downgraded from P1 to P2 — the suggested one-line fix (`sentiment_level ?? levelFromLegacy(sentiment)`) is correct and worth applying as consistency hygiene, but no user-visible badge-vs-facet divergence can occur in the Lab today.

title: saveBranches optimistic update never rolls back on failure — select shows unsaved value indefinitely
description: saveBranches sets onPos/onNeg state before the PATCH. On failure it sets an error banner but leaves the new value in the select. The re-sync effect deps are [group?.on_positive_action, group?.on_negative_action]; since the server values never changed, the effect never re-fires, so the select keeps displaying e.g. 'Notify me to take over' while the backend will still auto-draft. The user believes they changed reply handling when they didn't, until a full reload.
suggestion: In the catch block, restore the previous values (capture them before the optimistic set and setOnPos/setOnNeg back), or always re-sync from the mutateGroup() result after the request settles regardless of success.
verifyNote: Confirmed: saveBranches (page.tsx:132-141) sets onPos/onNeg before the PATCH and the catch only sets an error banner; the re-sync effect (page.tsx:105-108) deps are the unchanged server primitives so it never re-fires, and apiFetch throws on non-OK (client.ts:101), leaving the select stuck on the unsaved value. P2 is fair since it's failure-path-only and an error alert is shown. Fix caveat: the "re-sync via mutateGroup()" variant of the suggestion won't work (deps unchanged) — use the capture-previous-values-and-restore-in-catch approach, or explicitly setOnPos/setOnNeg from the awaited fresh group.

title: 'Replied' status chip is near-duplicate of the sentiment row and the numbers visibly disagree
description: Sentiment levels are only ever non-NULL on rows that have an inbound message, i.e. rows the 'Replied' predicate (`cc.status='replied' OR cv.last_direction='in'`) already matches — so the sentiment row is a strict breakdown of 'Replied'. Showing both as peer facets invites users to compare: replied=7 vs sum-of-sentiment=5 (legacy NULL-label rows make them disagree today), which reads as a bug. Selecting Replied + a sentiment is also always a no-op refinement.
suggestion: Present sentiment chips as a visual sub-group of 'Replied' (indented under it, or only shown when replied>0), or drop the standalone Replied chip and keep No reply / Cold / Advanced as the status row — sentiment selection already implies replied. At minimum, after fixing the legacy COALESCE the totals will reconcile.
verifyNote: Confirmed: the label is written only by the poller's inbound path (poller.go:196-209 → conversation/repository.go:280-287), so sentiment rows are effectively a breakdown of the Replied predicate (group/service.go:425,446-454), and migration 000025 has no backfill of the label from the legacy sentiment column, so replied > sum(sentiment) is real and visible in the peer facet rows (facet-filter-bar.tsx:69-98). One correction: "Replied + sentiment is always a no-op" is not strictly true — engine.go:200-203 mark_cold overwrites status='replied' and a later outbound flips last_direction, leaving labeled rows outside the Replied bucket — so prefer the sub-grouping/backfill fix over dropping the Replied chip; severity P2 is right since filter results themselves are correct.

title: Facet counts and email list come from two independent fetch cycles — transient mismatch window
description: Chip counts read group.facet_counts from the `/outreach/groups/{id}` SWR key while rows come from the separate `/emails` key; each polls on its own 10s timer with no coordination. The SSE inbound handler does call both mutateGroup() and mutateEmails() (85-90, verified — and use-outreach-events.ts keeps the callback fresh via ref), so the post-event gap is only two-request skew; but between events the independent poll phases can leave counts up to ~10s out of sync with visible rows (e.g. a new Positive badge appears in the list while the Positive chip count lags, or vice versa).
suggestion: Return facet_counts in the /emails response (computed in the same transaction/snapshot as the row query) and read counts from emailsData, or at least align both SWR keys' revalidation by mutating them together everywhere (already done for SSE; the 10s polls remain unsynchronized).
verifyNote: Confirmed: chip counts read group.facet_counts from the /outreach/groups/{id} key (page.tsx:326) while rows come from the separate /emails key, each with its own uncoordinated refreshInterval:10000 (page.tsx:74,79); the backend Emails() returns only rows (service.go:347-387, outreach.ts:313), and phases demonstrably drift (facets in the emails key at line 77 resets its timer; saveBranches/saveSteps at lines 137/189 mutate only the group key), so non-inbound server-side changes (sender worker, tag classifier) can leave counts up to ~10s stale vs visible rows. The SSE caveat is also accurate (page.tsx:85-90; use-outreach-events.ts:25-28). P2/smell is the right severity — transient, self-healing, cosmetic. Fix as suggested, noting counts in the /emails response must be computed unfiltered (FacetFilterBar shows counts for unselected values, facet-filter-bar.tsx:60-110) in the same transaction as the filtered row query.

title: Zero-count chip display differs between group page and sim (blank vs '0')
description: FacetChip renders the count only when `count != null`. The backend facetCounts always sets all five sentiment keys and four status keys (even when 0), so group-page chips show an explicit '0'. The sim counts map only inserts keys when at least one lead matches, so sim sentiment chips for empty levels render with no number at all. Same shared component, two different idle appearances — minor but noticeable since the sim explicitly advertises 'filter exactly like the live inbox'.
suggestion: Seed the sim counts map with all SENTIMENT_ORDER keys at 0 before tallying (one line in the useMemo), or change FacetChip to render `count ?? 0` so both surfaces show zeros uniformly.
verifyNote: Confirmed: FacetChip hides undefined but shows 0 (facet-filter-bar.tsx:38); backend always emits all sentiment/status keys including zeros (backend-go/internal/outreach/group/service.go:463-465) so group chips show "0", while the sim counts map inserts keys only on match (simulation/page.tsx:350-358) yet renders all SENTIMENT_ORDER chips (line 407), leaving zero-count sim chips blank. Cosmetic parity issue only — filter semantics match — so P2 stands; prefer seeding the sim counts map with SENTIMENT_ORDER at 0 over `count ?? 0` in FacetChip, which would also add "0" to intentionally-blank intent-tag chips.

title: Send silently discards the user's manual edits when a draft is pre-filled — server sends the stored draft body, UI promises "your edits will be sent"
description: handleSend always passes draft_message_id when a draft is loaded (conversation-thread.tsx:108), plus the current subject/body from the textarea. But SendMessage in service.go takes the OPPOSITE precedence: when req.DraftMessageID != nil it loads the stored draft row and uses draft.Subject/draft.BodyText (lines 167-172); req.Subject and req.Body are only used in the else branch (lines 175-178). So if the user edits the AI draft in the textarea and clicks Send, the ORIGINAL stored draft — not their edited text — is emailed to a real buyer. The UI explicitly states "Editing an AI draft — your edits will be sent." (line 299), so the user has no reason to suspect anything; the sent bubble afterwards shows the stored body, by which time the email is already out. RefineDraft does persist its result via UpdateMessageBody, so only AI-made changes survive — every manual keystroke is silently reverted.
suggestion: In SendMessage, prefer req.Subject/req.Body when non-empty and use the draft row only to mark it consumed (UPDATE to sent with the request body), e.g. `if req.Body != "" { body = req.Body }` after loading the draft. Alternatively have the frontend PATCH the draft body before sending. Add a regression test: edit a pre-filled draft, send, assert the channel payload contains the edited text.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:152-178 uses draft.Subject/draft.BodyText whenever req.DraftMessageID != nil and only falls back to req.Subject/req.Body in the else branch, while conversation-thread.tsx:107-112 always sends draft_message_id plus the edited text and line 299 promises "your edits will be sent" — so manual edits are silently discarded and the stale draft is emailed (RefineDraft at service.go:631 is the only path that persists changes). The suggested fix is right but must also update the draft row's subject/body in the isDraft UPDATE (service.go:246-252), which currently only sets external_id/status/sent_at, so the persisted message matches what was actually sent.

title: Adjust refines the server's stored draft, not the textarea — user's manual edits are destroyed and the AI works from an outdated body
description: Confirmed exactly as suspected: handleAdjust sends only {draft_id, instruction, remember} (redraftReply, outreach.ts:188-196). RefineDraft loads the draft row and sets PreviousDraft from draft.BodyText in the DB (service.go:570-573, used at :625). If the user manually edited the body textarea before clicking Adjust, (a) the AI refines the stale stored body, ignoring their edits, and (b) setBody(msg.body_text ?? "") at line 149 overwrites the textarea, silently destroying everything they typed. Pressing Enter in the Adjust input (line 248-253) makes accidental triggering easy. Two distinct losses: the AI output doesn't reflect the user's edits, and the edits themselves vanish with no undo.
suggestion: Send the current textarea value as previous_draft in the refine request and have RefineDraft prefer it over the stored row (also persisting it via UpdateMessageBody so DB and UI converge). Cheaper stopgap: track the last server draft body in state; if body !== that snapshot, disable Adjust with a tooltip like "You've edited this draft — adjusting will regenerate from your edited text" (or confirm before overwriting).
verifyNote: Confirmed: redraftReply sends only {draft_id, instruction, remember} (outreach.ts:188-196; refineDraftRequest at handler.go:324-328 has no body field), RefineDraft sets PreviousDraft from the stored draft.BodyText (service.go:570-573, 625), and setBody(msg.body_text) at conversation-thread.tsx:149 overwrites the textarea — so manual edits are both ignored by the AI and destroyed with no undo, while line 299 ("your edits will be sent") reinforces the false expectation. Minor overstatement: Enter-triggering (lines 248-253) still requires a non-empty instruction, so it isn't truly accidental, but the core loss path needs no accident. Fix as suggested: add optional previous_draft to the refine request, prefer it over draft.BodyText, and persist it via UpdateMessageBody so DB and UI converge.

title: Engine auto-draft never clears existing pending drafts — two pending_approval rows accumulate; the newer engine draft is invisible and the stale one wins the compose pre-fill
description: Only Service.DraftReply calls DeletePendingDrafts (service.go:328); the engine's draftReplyForApproval (engine.go:336-345, reply-branch auto_draft_reply) inserts a pending_approval row unconditionally. Sequence: user clicks AI draft (pending A) → buyer sends a new reply → engine auto-drafts pending B. ListMessages orders created_at ASC (repository.go:504), and the thread's `data.messages.find(m => m.status === "pending_approval")` (line 78) picks the OLDEST — so the compose box pre-fills A, a draft written BEFORE the new inbound, while B (the one actually answering the buyer) is invisible: filtered from bubbles (line 160) and never pre-filled. SendMessage does not delete leftover pendings, so after sending A, B lingers as an orphan and the [data] effect re-fills the compose box with it right after the user thinks they're done — a ghost draft that confuses and pollutes the DB.
suggestion: Call DeletePendingDrafts in engine.draftReplyForApproval before CreateMessage (mirroring DraftReply), and delete remaining pendings in SendMessage after a successful draft send. In the UI, prefer the NEWEST pending (find on a reversed list) and/or surface a badge when more than one pending exists.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:336-345 (draftReplyForApproval) creates a pending_approval row with no cleanup — grep shows service.go:328 (DraftReply) is the sole DeletePendingDrafts caller, and SendMessage (service.go:244-276) only flips the sent draft's own row, leaving orphans; with repository.go:504 ordering created_at ASC, conversation-thread.tsx:78 prefills the oldest pending while line 160 hides the newer one, and the [data] effect (lines 73-88) re-fills the orphan after send since draftMsgID is reset at line 114. Fix is correct as suggested; refinement: in SendMessage call DeletePendingDrafts after the draft row is updated to 'sent' (deletion is by status, so the sent message is then safe), and in the UI pick the newest pending.

title: SendMessage accepts any message ID as a 'draft' without checking status — a stale pre-fill can re-send an already-sent email
description: SendMessage finds the draft purely by ID (`if msgs[i].ID == *req.DraftMessageID`, service.go:158-163) with no status check — contrast RefineDraft, which verifies pending_approval/draft status (service.go:566-569). The frontend makes this reachable: the pre-fill effect depends only on [data] (line 88) and re-arms whenever `pending && !draftMsgID`. After handleSend clears draftMsgID/body and calls mutate(), any in-flight revalidation that started before the send (60s refreshInterval at line 41, SSE mutate at line 47, or the markConversationRead mutate at line 76) can resolve with pre-send data still showing the draft as pending — re-filling the compose box with the just-sent draft and re-arming draftMsgID. Clicking Send again then re-sends the same message through the channel (and rewrites its row to sent), emailing the buyer a duplicate.
suggestion: Server: reject non-pending rows in SendMessage (return 409 if draft.Status is not pending_approval/draft), matching RefineDraft's check. Client: guard the pre-fill effect against re-arming a message ID it has already sent (track consumed draft IDs), and only pre-fill when the compose body is empty.
verifyNote: Backend confirmed: SendMessage matches the draft by ID only (service.go:158-166) and the post-send UPDATE has no status guard (service.go:246-252), so a repeated draft_message_id re-sends an already-sent email — unlike RefineDraft's check at service.go:566-569. The specific frontend race described is wrong (SWR 2.4.1 discards in-flight revalidations once mutate() registers a newer fetch — FETCH[key][1] !== startAt check in swr/dist/index/index.mjs:415), but the duplicate send is still reachable: handleSend's catch (conversation-thread.tsx:116-117) keeps draftMsgID armed after a lost-response send, so a user retry duplicates the email; a stale-cache remount can also re-arm a sent draft ID. The suggested server-side 409 on non-pending status is the right and sufficient fix.

title: "Remember this for this brand" hides which brand, tags, and sentiment the lesson is scoped to — wrong-brand lessons (default-brand fallback) are invisible until Settings
description: The checkbox label names no brand. Server-side, brandForConv (service.go:828-840) resolves the campaign's brand but silently falls back to the user's DEFAULT brand when the conversation has no campaign or the lookup fails — RefineDraft then calls RememberLesson against that sp.ID (service.go:634-635). RememberLesson additionally snapshots the conversation's current tags and 3-value sentiment bucket as the match scope (loader.go:96-104). None of this is surfaced: a user adjusting a draft on a non-campaign inbox thread saves a lesson onto the default brand, scoped to tags/sentiment they never saw, and it then shapes future drafts for that brand. The mistake only becomes visible if they happen to open Settings → that brand → Learned reply lessons. This is a knock-on of the accepted default-brand fallback, not the fallback itself.
suggestion: Make the label dynamic: "Remember for [Brand name] — applies to [sentiment] replies tagged [tag chips]". The conversation detail response already includes tags and sentiment; expose the resolved brand (id+name) on GET /outreach/conversations/{id} (the server already resolves it for drafting). After saving, show a confirmation toast naming the brand with an undo/delete link.
verifyNote: Confirmed: the checkbox label is static (conversation-thread.tsx:272-280), RefineDraft saves the lesson against brandForConv's silently-resolved brand which falls back to the default brand or even a zero-UUID stub with the error discarded (service.go:583, 634-635, 816-840), and RememberLesson snapshots tags+sentiment invisible in the thread UI (loader.go:95-110); the only discovery surface is LearnedLessonsCard in Settings (sender-profile-editor.tsx:412-434). Suggested fix is sound except its premise that the detail response already includes tags/sentiment is wrong — GET /outreach/conversations/{id} returns only conversation+messages (handler.go:186-189; Conversation type lacks both), so the backend must expose resolved brand and sentiment on the detail endpoint (tags are available via GET /{id}/tags).

title: Simulation Lab silently injects the brand's real saved lessons into 'test' drafts — hidden state contradicts the playbook-only label
description: The config label reads "Reply playbook (test how standing instructions shape drafts)" (page.tsx:267), implying the typed playbook is what's being tested. But simGuidance (simulation/service.go:391-408) also loads ALL of the brand's production brand_reply_lessons via s.sender.ListLessons and injects every lesson matching the simulated reply's sentiment bucket + tags into the draft prompt (used at :274). Nothing in the UI hints at this. Consequences: a run with an empty playbook is not a clean baseline; two users (or the same user before/after saving lessons) get different sim results for identical configs and can't tell why; A/B-ing playbook wording is confounded by invisible guidance. Production parity is a fair design goal, but a 'Lab' that mixes in undisclosed state breaks the user's mental model of what they are testing.
suggestion: Disclose and control it: when a brand is selected, fetch and render its matching lessons read-only under the playbook editor ("+N saved lessons for this brand will also apply"), with a toggle 'Include saved brand lessons' (default on, persisted in the run's config snapshot). Also record in the run summary whether lessons were included so past runs stay interpretable.
verifyNote: Confirmed: simGuidance (backend-go/internal/outreach/simulation/service.go:398) live-loads the brand's production brand_reply_lessons (sender/repository.go:54-58) and injects matches into the sim draft prompt (service.go:274), while the simulation UI never mentions lessons anywhere (grep: "lesson" absent from frontend/src/app/(dashboard)/simulation/page.tsx; label at :267 frames the playbook as the sole variable). Fix suggestion is good; extend it to also snapshot the playbook in the run record, since service.go:50-52 shows the playbook is transient too, so past runs are doubly uninterpretable.

title: Playbook save silently drops empty-instruction rows and re-orders entries — user's in-progress rule vanishes under a "Playbook saved" message
description: SavePlaybook skips entries with blank instructions or invalid tags (group/service.go:230-233) and the handler responds with the post-save GetPlaybook, which the group page writes straight into state (setPlaybook(res.playbook), page.tsx:123). A user who clicked "Add rule" but hadn't typed the instruction yet sees their row disappear the moment they save, paired with the success message "Playbook saved" — it reads like data loss, not validation. GetPlaybook also returns ORDER BY tag (service.go:200), so saved rows silently re-sort alphabetically, breaking the user's authoring order. (Duplicate tags can't currently arise: the PlaybookEditor disables used tags, playbook-editor.tsx:44, and the server upserts last-write-wins on (campaign_id, tag), service.go:234-237.) The simulation page has the same silent filter client-side (page.tsx:111-113).
suggestion: Validate client-side before saving: highlight empty-instruction rows and block save with "Rule for [tag] has no instruction" (or explicitly confirm discarding). If server-side filtering stays, return a count of dropped entries so the UI can say "Saved 3 rules, 1 empty rule discarded".
verifyNote: Confirmed: SavePlaybook silently skips blank-instruction rows (service.go:230-233), the handler returns post-save GetPlaybook (handler.go:203-204) which page.tsx:122-124 writes into state under a "Playbook saved" message, and "Add rule" creates exactly such an empty row (playbook-editor.tsx:72); GetPlaybook's ORDER BY tag (service.go:200) re-sorts rows out of the editor's non-alphabetical INTENT_TAGS authoring order. P2 is correct since no typed content is ever lost (TrimSpace keeps any non-blank instruction); the suggested client-side validation in the shared PlaybookEditor flow is the right fix as it covers both the group page and the simulation page's identical silent filter (simulation/page.tsx:111-113).

title: Create-group dialog offers reply branches but no playbook, unlike the simulation config and group page
description: At creation time the dialog exposes the full automation surface — cadence steps (line 196-199) and both reply-branch selects (lines 201-225) — but not the reply playbook, which only becomes editable after creation on the group page (and notably IS available pre-run in the Simulation Lab config, simulation/page.tsx:266-269). Since the positive branch default is auto_draft_reply, the first inbound replies to a new group are drafted without any playbook guidance unless the user knows to navigate back to the group page and add one — an inconsistent mental model: 'how replies are handled' is configured at create, but 'what the reply should say' is not.
suggestion: Add an optional collapsed "Reply playbook" section to the dialog reusing PlaybookEditor, and pass entries in the createGroup payload (backend Create would persist into campaign_tag_guidance in the same transaction). Cheaper: after creation, route to the group page with the playbook card highlighted / a one-time hint.
verifyNote: Confirmed: create-group-dialog.tsx:196-225 configures cadence + reply branches but the createGroup payload (outreach.ts:233-241) has no playbook field, while simulation/page.tsx:266-269 offers PlaybookEditor pre-run and the group page only post-create ([groupId]/page.tsx:490-499); backend engine.go:210-211 + replyguidance/loader.go:30 confirm first positive-reply drafts run with empty campaign_tag_guidance. Playbook is optional and drafting still works, so P2 (parity/discoverability) is the right severity; the cheaper fix (post-create hint/highlight on the group page the dialog already routes to at line 87) is the better cost/benefit since the dialog-embed variant also requires backend Create changes (group/handler.go only has GET/PUT /playbook).

title: LearnedLessonsCard: unbounded lesson list and delete with no error handling
description: ListLessons has no LIMIT (sender/repository.go:54-58) and the card renders every row — since lessons are stored verbatim per adjust-with-remember, an active user accumulates an ever-growing settings card. remove() (lines 426-429) awaits deleteBrandLesson with no try/catch: a failed delete is an unhandled promise rejection and the row simply stays with zero feedback. On the staleness question: the cross-page SWR gap (thread saves a lesson; this card's key /outreach/sender-profile/{id}/lessons isn't mutated) is acceptable in practice because SWR revalidates on mount/focus when the user navigates to Settings — only a simultaneously-mounted card would show stale data. Note only the newest 6 lessons are ever injected into drafts (replyguidance/loader.go:16,51), which the card doesn't convey — users may believe all listed lessons apply.
suggestion: Wrap remove() in try/catch and surface failures (reuse the editor's msg Alert). Cap the initial render (e.g. 20 + "show all") or add server-side pagination. Indicate the injection limit, e.g. badge the 6 most recent per sentiment bucket as "active" so the verbatim-storage design stays predictable.
verifyNote: Confirmed: ListLessons has no LIMIT (backend-go/internal/outreach/sender/repository.go:55-58) and the card renders every row with no cap (sender-profile-editor.tsx:444-467); remove() at lines 426-429 awaits deleteBrandLesson without try/catch while apiFetch throws ApiError on non-OK (frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts:92-94) and no global unhandledrejection handler exists, so a failed delete gives zero feedback; lessonLimit=6 injection cap verified at replyguidance/loader.go:16,51 and is not conveyed by the card copy (lines 437-440). P2 is the honest severity (polish/error-handling gaps, happy path works). Suggested fix is good, but note the msg Alert lives in the parent SenderProfileEditor (line 48), so the card needs local error state or a lifted prop.

title: Simulation lead count: empty/out-of-range input is silently rewritten to 8 server-side
description: The Leads input uses Number(e.target.value), so clearing the field stores 0 (and the HTML min/max don't prevent typing 30 or 0). The server then silently replaces any LeadCount <= 0 or > 25 with 8 (simulation/service.go:69-71). The progress UI even initializes with the user's requested number (setProgress({done:0,total:leadCount}), page.tsx:100) before SSE corrects it, so a user who typed 30 watches "Running 0/30" jump to .../8 with no explanation, and the run consumes 8 AI-judged leads they didn't ask for.
suggestion: Clamp client-side on change/blur (1-25) and show the bound ("max 25"); have the server reject out-of-range values with a 400 instead of substituting a different number, or at minimum echo the adjusted count in the response so the UI can state "adjusted to 8".
verifyNote: Confirmed: page.tsx:181 stores Number(e.target.value) (empty field -> 0, min/max don't block typed 30), page.tsx:100 seeds progress with the raw count, and service.go:69-71 silently rewrites any out-of-range LeadCount to 8 with no handler validation (handler.go:72-81) — the SSE event (service.go:141) then publishes total=len(jobs), so "0/30" visibly jumps to "/8". P2 is honest since it only triggers on out-of-range input; the suggested fix (client clamp 1-25 + server 400 instead of substitution) is correct.

title: Manual edits to an AI draft are silently discarded on Send — stale draft body goes to the buyer
description: ConversationThread pre-fills the compose box from a pending_approval draft, sets draftMsgID, and shows 'Editing an AI draft — your edits will be sent.' handleSend passes BOTH draft_message_id and the edited subject/body. But Service.SendMessage ignores req.Subject/req.Body whenever req.DraftMessageID != nil — it reloads the stored draft and sends its stored subject/body verbatim. Any manual edits the user typed into the textarea (the primary way to fix an AI reply before approving) are silently dropped; the unedited AI text is emailed to a real buyer. Only edits made via the 'Adjust' (refine) flow survive, because RefineDraft persists to the stored row. This affects every engine-auto-drafted reply approval and every StartFromContact draft.
suggestion: In SendMessage, when DraftMessageID is set AND req.Subject/req.Body are non-empty, prefer the request values (and persist them onto the draft row before dispatch), or have the frontend PATCH the draft body (a draft-update endpoint already exists for campaign drafts) before calling send. Add a test: edit-then-send must deliver the edited body.
verifyNote: Confirmed: service.go:152-178 uses only the stored draft's subject/body when req.DraftMessageID != nil (req.Subject/req.Body read only in the else branch at 175-177), while conversation-thread.tsx:107-112 sends both and line 299 promises "your edits will be sent" — edits are silently dropped and the stale AI body is emailed to a real buyer (ch.Send, service.go:237); only RefineDraft persists edits via UpdateMessageBody (service.go:631), and even that only updates body, not subject. Fix as suggested: prefer non-empty req.Subject/req.Body when DraftMessageID is set and fold them into the existing draft-row UPDATE at service.go:246-251 so the persisted row matches what was sent.

title: Sequence cadence action 'mark_cold' permanently UNSUBSCRIBES the contact instead of marking cold
description: fireAction's SequenceActionMarkCold branch calls e.contacts.MarkUnsubscribed(ctx, conv.ContactID, "sequence_marked_cold"), which sets contacts.unsubscribed_at. Three knock-ons: (1) every non-replier in a cadence ending with mark_cold is treated as a legal opt-out forever — campaign/drafter.go:63-65 and scheduler.go:61-62 skip unsubscribed contacts, so these leads are permanently excluded from ALL future email groups with no UI to undo it; (2) the contact detail page shows the red 'unsubscribed' compliance badge for someone who merely went silent; (3) it never sets campaign_contacts.status='cold', so the group's Cold facet/status doesn't reflect it (row stays 'sent' / 'no_reply'). This contradicts the reply-branch mark_cold (engine.go:201-203, sets status='cold' only) and the Simulation Lab, whose cadence mark_cold (simulation/service.go:315-318) produces outcome 'cold', not 'unsubscribed' — so the Lab does not mirror what production actually does here.
suggestion: Change the cadence mark_cold action to UPDATE campaign_contacts SET status='cold' WHERE conversation_id=$1 (and optionally set pipeline_stage='lost'), reserving MarkUnsubscribed strictly for compliance routes (unsubscribe tag, keyword opt-out, one-click handler). Audit existing rows with unsubscribe_reason='sequence_marked_cold' for backfill.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:371-372 routes the cadence mark_cold action to contacts.MarkUnsubscribed (repository.go:429-438, one-way COALESCE on unsubscribed_at with no resubscribe path anywhere), permanently suppressing non-repliers from all future outreach (drafter.go:63-65, scheduler.go:61-62 via IsSuppressed at unsubscribe.go:101-103) and showing the compliance 'unsubscribed' badge (contacts/[contactId]/page.tsx:97-99), while the reply-branch mark_cold (engine.go:200-203) and Simulation Lab (simulation/service.go:315-318) both treat the same action as status='cold' — and the builder's own help text (followup-actions.ts:16) promises 'moves the contact to cold'. P0 stands: irreversible production data corruption on a default-shaped cadence path; the suggested fix (UPDATE campaign_contacts SET status='cold' WHERE conversation_id=$1, reserve MarkUnsubscribed for compliance routes, backfill unsubscribe_reason='sequence_marked_cold' rows) is correct and the reason column makes the backfill safely identifiable.

title: Keyword-unsubscribed contacts can still get an auto-drafted reply and be emailed on approval — suppression check missing on the reply-draft/approve path
description: Dual-path conflict: the poller suppresses on opt-out keywords (compliance.LooksLikeOptOut → MarkUnsubscribed 'reply_keyword') but then still wakes the sequence run (poller.go:212-215). When the classifier missed the 'unsubscribe' intent tag (the keyword matcher and the AI tagger are independent), handleReplyBranch falls through to the sentiment branch; for neutral/positive sentiment, draftReplyForApproval drafts a reply for a contact who just opted out — it checks PrimaryEmail but never compliance.IsSuppressed. The user then approves it via conversation.Service.SendMessage, which also has no suppression check (and appends no unsubscribe footer), so the opted-out contact gets emailed. The scheduler's comment ('campaign sends ALWAYS go through this gate, never the bare conversation.SendMessage path') is false for engine-drafted replies — they are sent through exactly that bare path. The engine's auto-send path (actionSendMessage:416-418) DOES check IsSuppressed, making the inconsistency clear.
suggestion: Add a compliance.IsSuppressed check at the top of handleReplyBranch (treat as RouteSuppress: set cc status='cold', stop the run) and a defensive check in conversation.Service.SendMessage that refuses outbound sends to suppressed contacts unless an explicit override flag is set.
verifyNote: Confirmed end-to-end: poller.go:226-230 keyword-suppresses (contacts.unsubscribed_at only — repository.go:429 doesn't close the conversation) yet poller.go:212-215 wakes the run; handleReplyBranch routes solely on AI tags (trigger.go:66-85; classifyReply returns zero tags on AI error, poller.go:250-263), so a missed unsubscribe tag falls to the neutral/positive branch and draftReplyForApproval (engine.go:288-291) checks only PrimaryEmail — never compliance.IsSuppressed — while sibling actionSendMessage does (engine.go:416). Approval flows through conversation.Service.SendMessage (service.go:139-304, frontend conversation-thread.tsx sendMessage with draft_message_id), which has no suppression check and no compliance footer, falsifying scheduler.go:21-22's "never the bare conversation.SendMessage path" claim. Suggested fix is right; additionally re-check IsSuppressed inside SendMessage immediately before ch.Send (per compliance/unsubscribe.go:99's own contract) since suppression can occur between draft and approval on any path. P1 not P0: send still requires explicit human approval plus an AI-tag miss, so no unconditional auto-send to suppressed contacts.

title: Group cold-email drafts have no 'Adjust by prompting' — refine affordance unreachable for the entire pre-send approval flow
description: Mapping of pending-draft surfaces: (a) engine auto-drafted replies → expanded 'Replied' row renders ConversationThread (has Adjust + remember-lesson); (b) StartFromContact drafts → /outreach/[conversationId] thread (has Adjust); (c) campaign cold drafts awaiting approval → GroupDraftEditor only — a manual subject/body textarea with Save / Save & approve, no AI-adjust input and no remember-as-lesson option. There is no alternate route to the thread for these rows: the group page renders GroupDraftEditor whenever status==='drafted', the standalone inbox is gone (/outreach redirects to groups), and the nested groups/[groupId]/[conversationId] route is linked from nowhere. The backend already supports this: RefineDraft accepts messages in status 'draft' as well as 'pending_approval' (conversation/service.go:566-568), so this is purely missing UI wiring — the largest-volume drafting surface (bulk cold emails) is the only one without the new iterate-with-AI capability.
suggestion: Add the same adjust-instruction input (+ remember checkbox) to GroupDraftEditor, calling redraftReply(conversationId, {draft_id, instruction}) and refreshing the textarea from the response. Note RefineDraft currently hardcodes Mode 'reply'; pass/derive a cold-draft mode for these (see separate finding).
verifyNote: Confirmed: GroupDraftEditor (group-draft-editor.tsx:57-126) has only Save/Save & approve with no redraftReply wiring, the group page renders it for every status==='drafted' row (groups/[groupId]/page.tsx:398-409), /outreach redirects to groups (outreach/page.tsx:6), nothing links to the nested groups/[groupId]/[conversationId] route, and the backend already accepts status 'draft' in RefineDraft (conversation/service.go:566-568) while hardcoding Mode "reply" (service.go:615). The suggested fix is right and necessary — ConversationThread would not help even if linked, since it only arms Adjust for status==='pending_approval' drafts (conversation-thread.tsx:78), while campaign cold drafts are created as 'draft' (campaign/drafter.go:148).

title: Engine-drafted pending replies are invisible in the group email list — no 'draft awaiting approval' indicator or facet
description: When the positive branch auto-drafts a reply, the message sits at pending_approval, but nothing in the group page tells the user it exists: the row's badge shows only 'Replied' (cc.status), GroupEmail carries no has_pending_draft field, facetCounts has no needs-approval bucket, and Notifications are created only for notify/wrong_contact routes. The draft is discoverable only by manually expanding each replied row (ConversationThread then pre-fills it). For the product's core loop — 'engine drafts, user approves' — drafts can silently age out of relevance. Contrast: cold-email drafts get an explicit 'Awaiting approval' badge + Approve button on the same list.
suggestion: Add an EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM messages m WHERE m.conversation_id=cv.id AND m.status='pending_approval') boolean to the Emails query and a needs_approval facet count; render a distinct badge ('Reply drafted — review') and surface it in the group header/notifications panel.
verifyNote: Confirmed: engine.go:211→344 creates a pending_approval reply with no task (notify routes at engine.go:188/199/209 do create tasks), group/service.go:76-91 GroupEmail has no pending-draft field and facetCounts (444-487) has no needs-approval bucket, and the group page badge (page.tsx:373-375) shows only cc.status ('Replied') with the Approve button gated on status==='drafted'; conversation-thread.tsx:78-82 surfaces the draft only after manual row expansion. Suggested fix is correct; a cheaper alternative is creating a task in draftReplyForApproval so the existing 'Needs attention' panel surfaces it, but the EXISTS column + needs_approval facet + badge is the better UX.

title: Pre-scoring conversations show a sentiment badge but are excluded from the matching sentiment facet and its count
description: Knock-on of the accepted no-backfill trade-off: SentimentBadge falls back to levelFromLegacy(legacy) so a historical row (last_inbound_sentiment='positive', label NULL) renders a 'Positive' badge in the group list. But the backend facet filter matches only cv.last_inbound_sentiment_label = ANY(...) and facetCounts FILTERs on the same label column — both NULL for those rows. Result: the user sees a Positive-badged row, the Positive chip count doesn't include it, and clicking 'Positive' makes the row disappear. Display and filter disagree on the same screen.

title: Score boundary ±0.2: UI label says Neutral while the engine branches Negative (mark cold) / Positive
description: LabelForScore treats exactly -0.2 and 0.2 as 'neutral' (negative is score < -0.2; neutral is <= 0.2), but LegacyForScore — which the reply branch keys off via conversations.last_inbound_sentiment (engine.go:260-264) — treats -0.2 as 'negative' and 0.2 as 'positive' (inclusive bounds). Classifiers frequently emit round values like ±0.2, so a reply can display a Neutral badge while the engine marks the contact cold (at -0.2) or auto-drafts an engage reply (at +0.2). The unit tests assert both behaviors, so the cross-function disagreement is baked in rather than accidental in either function alone.
suggestion: Align the inclusive/exclusive bounds: make LegacyForScore use score > 0.2 → positive and score < -0.2 → negative (matching LabelForScore), update the two boundary test cases, and re-derive stored legacy values with one UPDATE from sentiment_score.

One overstatement: the +0.2 side is behaviorally inert because ResolveReplyBranch (engine.go:235-240) routes neutral down the positive/auto-draft branch anyway, so the real conflict is only the -0.2/mark-cold case (plus a minor lesson-matching mismatch in replyguidance/loader.go:85-91). Suggested fix is correct: make LegacyForScore strict (score > 0.2 / score < -0.2), update the two boundary tests, and re-derive stored last_inbound_sentiment from last_inbound_sentiment_score with one UPDATE; simulation/aicalls.go:88-89 inherits the fix automatically.

title: RefineDraft always runs in Mode 'reply' — wrong prompt/guard for cold openers and followups, and drops the signature guarantee
description: RefineDraft accepts drafts in status 'draft' or 'pending_approval' (so cold campaign drafts and engine followups qualify) but unconditionally builds prompts.OutreachReplyInput{Mode: "reply"}. For an initial cold draft (e.g., StartFromContact pending draft, or group drafts once finding #4 is wired) every non-draft message is filtered out, so the AI is told to 'reply' to an empty conversation; for followup drafts the guard runs in reply mode, which flags phrases ('circle back'/'touch base') that followup mode deliberately tolerates, burning a StricterRetry. Also, unlike draftInitialMessage (line 399) the refined body is persisted without prompts.WithSignature, so refining an initial draft can strip the brand signature the original draft was guaranteed to have.

P2 is right (draft-quality/retry waste, user still reviews before send). Fix as suggested, but note BuildOutreachReplyPrompt has no "initial" mode (outreach_reply.go:132-138) — initial-state refines need an extended prompt mode or the draft-prompt path, plus idempotent WithSignature re-application.
